title.en: Volume 438 Biographies 197: Confucian Scholars 8 - Tang Han, He Ji, Wang Bai, Xu Mengshen and younger brothers: Dezhi, nephew: Tianlin, Li Xinchuan, Ye Weidao, Wang Yinglin, Huang Zhen
title.raw: 卷四百三十八 列傳第一百九十七 儒林八 湯漢 何基 王柏 徐夢莘弟:得之 從子:天麟 李心傳 葉味道 王應麟 黃震 Volume 438 Biographies 197: Confucian Scholars 8 - Tang Han, He Ji, Wang Bai, Xu Mengshen and younger brothers: Dezhi, nephew: Tianlin, Li Xinchuan, Ye Weidao, Wang Yinglin, Huang Zhen

sentences.zh: 儒林八

translations.literal: Confucian Scholars 8
translations.idiomatic: Confucian Scholars, Part Eight

sentences.zh: ○湯漢何基王柏徐夢莘

translations.literal: ○ Tang Han, He Ji, Wang Bai, Xu Mengshen
translations.idiomatic: Tang Han, He Ji, Wang Bai, and Xu Mengshen

sentences.zh: （弟得之從子天麟附）〉

translations.literal: (Younger brother Dezhi and nephew Tianlin appended)
translations.idiomatic: (with the younger brother Dezhi and the nephew Tianlin appended)

sentences.zh: 李心傳葉味道王應麟黃震

translations.literal: Li Xinchuan, Ye Weidao, Wang Yinglin, Huang Zhen
translations.idiomatic: Li Xinchuan, Ye Weidao, Wang Yinglin, and Huang Zhen

sentences.zh: 湯漢，字伯紀，饒州安仁人。

translations.literal: Tang Han, styled Boji, was a native of Anren in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Han, courtesy name Boji, came from Anren in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 與其兄幹、巾、中皆知名當時，柴中行見而奇之。

translations.literal: He and his elder brothers Gan, Jin, and Zhong were all renowned in their day; Chai Zhongxing saw them and regarded them as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brothers Gan, Jin, and Zhong were all famous in their time; when Chai Zhongxing met them, he was struck by their talent.

sentences.zh: 真德秀在潭，致漢為賓客。

translations.literal: When Zhen Dexiu was in Tanzhou, he invited Han as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhen Dexiu was serving in Tanzhou, he brought Han on as a house guest.

sentences.zh: 嚐造趙汝談，汝談曰：“第一流也。

translations.literal: He once visited Zhao Rutan, and Rutan said, "A man of the first rank."
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he called on Zhao Rutan, who declared, "This is a man of the first rank."

sentences.zh: ”江東提刑趙汝騰薦漢於朝，詔免解差，充象山書院堂長。

translations.literal: " Zhao Ruteng, judicial intendant of Jiangdong, recommended Han to the court; an edict exempted him from the qualifying examination and appointed him head lecturer of Xiangshan Academy.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhao Ruteng, the judicial intendant of Jiangdong, recommended Han to the court; the throne exempted him from the qualifying examination and named him head lecturer of Xiangshan Academy.

sentences.zh: 赴禮部別院試，正奏名，授上饒縣主簿。

translations.literal: He took the separate-branch examination at the Ministry of Rites, was entered on the main list of graduates, and was appointed chief clerk of Shangrao County.
translations.idiomatic: He sat for the separate-branch examination at the Ministry of Rites, passed on the main roll, and received appointment as chief clerk of Shangrao County.

sentences.zh: 江東轉運使趙希塈言：“漢，今海內知名士也，豈得吏之州縣哉！

translations.literal: Zhao Xichong, transport commissioner of Jiangdong, said, "Han is a scholar famous throughout the realm today—how can he be made a petty county official!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xichong, transport commissioner of Jiangdong, protested, "Han is among the most celebrated scholars in the empire—how can he be relegated to routine service in a prefecture or county!"

sentences.zh: ”詔循兩資，差信州教授兼象山書院長。

translations.literal: " An edict counted both qualifications toward promotion and assigned him professor of Xinzhou while also making him director of Xiangshan Academy.
translations.idiomatic: " The court ordered his two qualifications counted together for promotion and posted him as professor at Xinzhou while also appointing him director of Xiangshan Academy.

sentences.zh: 淳祐十二年，差充史館校勘，改國史實錄院校勘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Chunyou he was assigned as collator in the Historiography Institute and then transferred to collator in the Veritable Records Institute for the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In 1252 he was detailed as collator in the Historiography Institute and soon transferred to collator in the Veritable Records Institute for the National History.

sentences.zh: 會大水，上封事曰：“君心敬肆之分，實上天喜怒之由。

translations.literal: When great floods occurred, he submitted a sealed memorial saying, "The distinction in the ruler's mind between reverence and license is in truth the source of Heaven's favor and wrath."
translations.idiomatic: When severe flooding struck, he submitted a sealed memorial: "Whether the sovereign's heart inclines to reverence or to license is precisely what moves Heaven to show favor or anger."

sentences.zh: 一念之敬，上帝臨汝，祥風慶雲所從出也。

translations.literal: "A single thought of reverence—'The Lord on High is watching you'—and auspicious winds and celebratory clouds issue forth."
translations.idiomatic: "A single reverent thought—'The Lord on High is upon you'—and the auspicious winds and felicitous clouds will follow."

sentences.zh: 一念之肆，上帝震怒，妖浸陰沴所從生也。

translations.literal: "A single thought of license—'The Lord on High is enraged'—and demonic inundations and yin malignities are born."
translations.idiomatic: "A single licentious thought—'The Lord on High is enraged'—and demonic floods and yin pestilence take root."

sentences.zh: ”火災，應詔上封事曰：

translations.literal: " When fire broke out, in response to an imperial summons he submitted a sealed memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: " When fire broke out, he answered an imperial summons with another sealed memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞任天下之大，立心不可不公；

translations.literal: "Your subject has heard that in bearing the great charge of All under Heaven, the heart set in office must not be other than fair;
translations.idiomatic: "Your subject has heard that whoever bears the great charge of the realm must set his heart on nothing but fairness;

sentences.zh: 守天下之重，持心不可不敬。

translations.literal: in guarding the weighty trust of All under Heaven, the heart upheld must not be other than reverent.
translations.idiomatic: and whoever guards its weighty trust must uphold his heart in reverence.

sentences.zh: 陛下膺皇天之眷命，受祖宗之寶圖，則不當懷私恩；

translations.literal: Your Majesty has received Heaven's favoring mandate and inherited the precious chart of the ancestors—therefore private favor must not be cherished;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has received Heaven's favoring mandate and inherited the ancestral patrimony—you must not harbor private favor;

sentences.zh: 為天下共主，為億兆寄命，則不當隆私親。

translations.literal: as common sovereign of All under Heaven and as the one to whom hundreds of millions entrust their lives, private kin must not be exalted.
translations.idiomatic: as sovereign of all the world and as the one on whom the myriad people stake their lives, you must not elevate private kin.

sentences.zh: 大臣邇臣，服休服采，皆陛下所倚仗也，則不當信私人。

translations.literal: Great ministers and near ministers, in court dress and in mourning dress, are all those on whom Your Majesty relies—therefore private persons must not be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers and the intimate attendants, whether in court regalia or in mourning garb, are all men Your Majesty should rely upon—you must not put your faith in private favorites.

sentences.zh: 三省、密院者，陛下之朝廷，發號布政所從出也，則不當有私令。

translations.literal: The Three Departments and the Privy Council are Your Majesty's court, whence orders issue and government is proclaimed—therefore there must be no private commands.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments and the Privy Council are Your Majesty's court, the source from which decrees issue and policy is proclaimed—there must be no private orders.

sentences.zh: 四海九州，土宇反章，皆陛下之倉廩府庫也，則不當殖私財。

translations.literal: Within the four seas and nine provinces, every inch of land and every pattern of the realm are Your Majesty's granaries and treasuries—therefore private wealth must not be amassed.
translations.idiomatic: All the land within the four seas and nine provinces is Your Majesty's granary and treasury—you must not hoard private wealth.

sentences.zh: 陛下於皇天祖宗之德弗永念，而報答私恩；

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not keep forever in mind the virtue of Heaven and the ancestors, but instead repays private favor;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty does not keep constantly in mind the virtue owed to Heaven and the ancestors, but repays private obligations instead;

sentences.zh: 於群黎百姓之疾苦弗深恤，而富貴私親；

translations.literal: does not deeply pity the suffering of the myriad people, but enriches and ennobles private kin;
translations.idiomatic: does not deeply pity the suffering of the common people, but enriches and ennobles private kin;

sentences.zh: 公卿在廷，其信任不若近習之篤；

translations.literal: the trust placed in dukes and ministers at court is not as deep as that placed in intimate favorites;
translations.idiomatic: the trust placed in the dukes and ministers at court is not as deep as that placed in intimate favorites;

sentences.zh: 中書造命，其除行不若內批之專，則陛下之立心，既未能盡合乎天下之公矣。

translations.literal: when the Secretariat drafts appointments, their promulgation is not as exclusive as inner drafts—thus Your Majesty's heart set in office has already failed to accord fully with the fairness owed to All under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: when the Secretariat drafts appointments, their promulgation is not as absolute as the emperor's inner drafts—thus Your Majesty's heart has already failed to accord fully with the public good of the realm.

sentences.zh: 往者陛下上畏天戒，下恤人言，內則拘製於權臣，外則恐怯於強敵，敬心既不敢盡弛，則私意亦未得盡行。

translations.literal: Formerly Your Majesty feared Heaven's warnings above and pitied popular opinion below; inwardly you were constrained by powerful ministers, outwardly you feared strong enemies—since reverent caution dared not be wholly relaxed, private intent likewise could not be wholly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier years Your Majesty feared Heaven's warnings above and heeded popular opinion below; inwardly you were hemmed in by powerful ministers, outwardly you shrank before strong enemies—because reverence could not be wholly abandoned, private desires could not be wholly indulged either.

sentences.zh: 比年以來，天戒人言既以玩熟，而貪濁柄國，贖貨無厭，彼既將恣行其私，則不得不縱陛下之所欲為。

translations.literal: In recent years Heaven's warnings and popular opinion have been treated with familiarity and contempt, while the greedy and corrupt hold power and are insatiable in taking bribes—since they were about to indulge their private aims without restraint, they had no choice but to let Your Majesty do as you pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years Heaven's warnings and public criticism have been treated with contempt, while greedy, corrupt men hold power and are insatiable for bribes—since they intended to pursue their private aims without restraint, they had no choice but to indulge whatever Your Majesty wished to do.

sentences.zh: 於是前日之敬畏盡忘，而一念之私始四出而不可禦矣。

translations.literal: Thus the reverent caution of former days was wholly forgotten, and a single private thought began to issue on every side and could no longer be checked.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the reverence of former days was wholly forgotten, and private impulses began to burst forth on every side beyond all control.

sentences.zh: 姑以近事跡之：定策之碑，忽從中出，鄉未欲親其文也；

translations.literal: Take recent events as proof: the stele commemorating the settlement of the succession suddenly issued from within the palace—formerly you did not wish to read its text yourself;
translations.idiomatic: Consider recent events: the stele commemorating the settlement of the succession suddenly issued from within the palace—formerly you would not even read its text yourself;

sentences.zh: 貴戚子弟，參錯中外，鄉不如是之放也；

translations.literal: sons and younger brothers of the imperial kin were mixed throughout court and provinces—formerly they were not so unrestrained;
translations.idiomatic: kinsmen of the imperial clan were scattered through court and provinces—formerly they were not so unrestrained;

sentences.zh: 土木之禍，展轉流毒，訟牒細故，胥吏賤人皆得藉群榼之勢，徹清都之邃，鄉不如是之熾也；

translations.literal: the calamity of construction projects spread poison in turn; in petty lawsuits even clerks and base men could borrow the power of factional wine-jars to penetrate the deepest recesses of the pure capital—formerly it was not so fierce;
translations.idiomatic: the scourge of construction projects spread harm in every direction; in petty lawsuits even clerks and men of the lowest rank could borrow factional power to penetrate the innermost halls of government—formerly things were not so extreme;

sentences.zh: 御筆之出，上則廢朝令，下則侵有司，鄉不如是之多也；

translations.literal: when imperial brush-notes issued forth, above they voided court orders, below they encroached on the regular offices—formerly there were not so many;
translations.idiomatic: imperial brush-notes voided court orders above and encroached on the regular offices below—formerly there were not nearly so many;

sentences.zh: 賄賂之通，書致之操，鄉不如是其章也。

translations.literal: the channels of bribery and the control of written communications—formerly they were not so blatant.
translations.idiomatic: the channels of bribery and the manipulation of correspondence—formerly they were not so brazen.

sentences.zh: 故凡陛下之所以未能任大守重，而至於召怨宿禍者，始於立心之未公，成於持心之不敬，私以為主，而肆以行之。

translations.literal: Therefore, in all the reasons Your Majesty has been unable to bear the great charge and guard the weighty trust, until you have summoned resentment and stored up calamity—the beginning lay in a heart not set fairly in office, the completion in a heart not upheld reverently: taking the private as sovereign and acting with license.
translations.idiomatic: Thus everything that has kept Your Majesty from bearing the great charge and guarding the weighty trust, until resentment and stored-up calamity have been summoned, began with a heart not set on fairness and was completed in a heart not upheld in reverence—treating private interest as paramount and acting without restraint.

sentences.zh: 此所以感動天地，而水火之災捷出於數月之內也。

translations.literal: This is why Heaven and Earth were moved, and why flood and fire disasters swiftly appeared within a few months.
translations.idiomatic: This is why Heaven and Earth have been stirred, and why flood and fire have struck again within a few short months.

sentences.zh: 陛下得不亟為治亂持危之計，而可復以常日玩易之心處之乎！

translations.literal: Can Your Majesty fail to press forward at once with plans to order chaos and sustain peril—and yet again treat these matters with the careless ease of ordinary days!
translations.idiomatic: Can Your Majesty fail to press forward at once with plans to order chaos and sustain peril—and yet treat these matters with the same careless ease as on ordinary days!

sentences.zh: 授太學博士，轉對，言：“太祖之天下壞其半者，蔡京、王黼也。

translations.literal: Appointed Erudite of the Imperial University, he presented a rotating memorial saying, "Those who ruined half of Taizu's empire were Cai Jing and Wang Fu."
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Erudite of the Imperial University, he presented a rotating memorial: "Those who ruined half of Taizu's empire were Cai Jing and Wang Fu."

sentences.zh: 高宗之天下壞其半者，鄭清之也。

translations.literal: "Those who ruined half of Gaozong's empire was Zheng Qingzhi."
translations.idiomatic: "Those who ruined half of Gaozong's empire was Zheng Qingzhi."

sentences.zh: ”又曰：“苟有誌焉，則其紀綱必先正，其根本必先強，其藩籬必先固。

translations.literal: " He also said, "If one truly has the will, then its laws and standards must first be set right, its roots must first be strengthened, and its outer defenses must first be made firm."
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "If the ruler truly has the will, he must first set right the laws and standards, strengthen the foundations, and secure the outer defenses."

sentences.zh: 夫然後心廣體胖，泮渙而優遊，其樂無極矣。

translations.literal: "Only then will the mind be broad and the person at ease, expansive and unhurried in pleasure, with joy without limit."
translations.idiomatic: "Only then will the mind expand and the person be at ease, free to move in spacious leisure with joy without limit."

sentences.zh: 舍此不務，而徒以九重之深、一笑之適以為樂。

translations.literal: "To abandon this and pursue nothing but the depth of the ninefold palace and the pleasure of a single smile as one's joy.
translations.idiomatic: "To abandon this and seek joy only in the seclusion of the inner palace and the pleasure of a moment's smile.

sentences.zh: 樂極而思之，吾有朝廷而不能治也，吾有黎民而無與保之也，起視四境，而外侮又至矣。

translations.literal: When joy reaches its limit and one reflects: I have a court yet cannot govern it; I have the people yet have none with whom to preserve them; I rise and look to the four borders, and external insult has come again.
translations.idiomatic: When joy reaches its limit and one reflects: I have a court yet cannot govern it; I have the people yet cannot protect them; I rise and look to the four borders, and external aggression is upon us again.

sentences.zh: 雖有鄭、衛之音，燕、趙之色，建章之麗，瓊林之積，亦獨何樂哉！

translations.literal: Even with the music of Zheng and Wei, the beauties of Yan and Zhao, the splendor of Jianzhang, and the hoard of Qionglin—what joy is there alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Even with the music of Zheng and Wei, the beauties of Yan and Zhao, the splendor of Jianzhang Palace, and the treasures of Qionglin—what joy can there be in that alone!"

sentences.zh: 召試館職，遷秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Summoned to examination for a post in the academies, he was promoted to collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to examination for an academy post, he was promoted to collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 皇太子冠，差充太常博士，引賓讚，受命進《冠箴》，詔令太子拜謝。

translations.literal: When the crown prince came of age, Han was assigned as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to lead the guest and intone praise; receiving the order, he presented the 《Admonition at the Capping》; an edict directed the crown prince to bow in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: At the crown prince's capping ceremony, he was assigned as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to lead the guest and intone praise; ordered to present the 《Admonition at the Capping》, he did so, and an edict directed the crown prince to bow in thanks.

sentences.zh: 升秘書郎，轉對，極言邊事，以為：“今日扶危救亂無復他策，在乎人主清心無欲，盡用天下之財力以治兵。

translations.literal: Promoted to secretary, he presented a rotating memorial speaking at length on frontier affairs, holding that "today to support peril and rescue disorder there is no other plan: it lies in the ruler purifying his heart and being without desire, and employing all the wealth and strength of the realm to train troops."
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to secretary, he presented a rotating memorial on frontier affairs, arguing that "today there is no other way to support a state in peril and rescue it from disorder: the ruler must purify his heart and be without desire, and devote all the realm's wealth and strength to the army."

sentences.zh: 大臣公心無我，盡用天下之人才以強本，庶幾尚有以亡為存之理耳。

translations.literal: "Great ministers must have public hearts without self-interest and employ all the talent of the realm to strengthen the foundation—then perhaps there may still be the principle of turning extinction into survival."
translations.idiomatic: "Great ministers must serve with public hearts free of self-interest and employ all the realm's talent to strengthen the foundations—only then may there still be hope of turning extinction into survival."

sentences.zh: 提舉福建常平，劾福州守史岩之、泉州守謝。

translations.literal: As intendant of the Fujian Ever-Normal Granaries, he impeached Shi Yanzhi, prefect of Fuzhou, and Xie Hong, prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As intendant of the Fujian Ever-Normal Granaries, he impeached Shi Yanzhi, prefect of Fuzhou, and Xie Hong, prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 召為禮部郎官兼太子侍讀。

translations.literal: Summoned as a director in the Ministry of Rites while also serving as reader to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as a director in the Ministry of Rites and as reader to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 尋以直華文閣、福建運判，改知寧國府。

translations.literal: Soon granted directorship of the Huawen Pavilion and made transport judge of Fujian, then transferred to prefect of Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was granted directorship of the Huawen Pavilion and appointed transport judge of Fujian, then transferred to prefect of Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 遷提舉江西常平兼知吉州。

translations.literal: Transferred to intendant of the Jiangxi Ever-Normal Granaries while also serving as prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to intendant of the Jiangxi Ever-Normal Granaries while also serving as prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 移江東運判、知隆興府。

translations.literal: Moved to transport judge of Jiangdong and prefect of Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to transport judge of Jiangdong and prefect of Longxing.

sentences.zh: 召為尚左郎官兼太子侍讀、兼玉牒所檢討官，入奏：“願陛下端本澄源，虛己盡下，恢大公之道，開不諱之門，使朝廷之上，光明洞達，而無邪孽之根以撓其正。

translations.literal: Summoned as a director in the Left Office of the Ministry of Revenue while also reader to the crown prince and reviser at the Imperial Genealogy Office, he entered court and memorialized: "I wish Your Majesty would rectify the root and clarify the source, empty yourself and exhaust your humility, restore the great way of fairness, and open the gate of frank speech, so that above the court all is bright and penetrating, with no roots of evil to bend what is upright."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as a director in the Left Office of the Ministry of Revenue, reader to the crown prince, and reviser at the Imperial Genealogy Office, he entered court and said: "I pray Your Majesty will rectify the root and clarify the source, empty yourself and heed all below, restore the great way of fairness, and open the gate of frank speech, so that the court may be bright and penetrating, with no roots of evil to bend what is upright."

sentences.zh: 四海之內，歡欣交通，而無怨戾之氣以奸其和。

translations.literal: "Within the four seas, joy and communication prevail, with no resentful, rebellious air to violate harmony."
translations.idiomatic: "Within the four seas, joy and mutual trust may prevail, with no resentful, rebellious spirit to violate harmony."

sentences.zh: 臣之忠愛，莫切於此。

translations.literal: "In your subject's loyal devotion, nothing is more urgent than this."
translations.idiomatic: "In your subject's loyal devotion, nothing is more urgent than this."

sentences.zh: 遷太府少卿，升兼太子諭德，改秘書少監。

translations.literal: Transferred to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, then promoted to concurrent tutor to the crown prince and changed to vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, then promoted to concurrent tutor to the crown prince and appointed vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 疏論：“比年董宋臣聲焰薰灼，其力能去台諫，排大臣，結連凶渠，惡德參會，以致兵戈相尋之禍。

translations.literal: In a memorial he argued: "In recent years Dong Songchen's prestige has blazed forth; his power could remove censors and remonstrators, displace great ministers, join with vicious ringleaders, and combine wicked conduct, bringing on the calamity of unending warfare."
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he argued: "In recent years Dong Songchen's prestige has blazed forth; his power could remove censors and remonstrators, displace great ministers, join with vicious ringleaders, and combine every kind of wicked conduct, bringing on the calamity of unending warfare."

sentences.zh: 陛下灼見其故，斥而遠之，臣意其影滅而跡絕矣。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty clearly saw the cause, expelled him and kept him at a distance—I thought his shadow had vanished and his tracks were gone."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty clearly saw the cause, expelled him and kept him at a distance—I thought his shadow had vanished and his tracks were gone forever."

sentences.zh: 豈料夫陰消而再凝，冰解而驟合，既得自便，即圖復用，以其罪戾之餘，一旦復使之出入壺奧之中，給事宗廟之內，此其重幹神人之怒，再基禍亂之源，上下皇惑，大小切齒。

translations.literal: "Who could have expected that yin once dispersed would congeal again, that ice once melted would suddenly reunite? Once he regained his ease, he at once plotted reuse; with the dregs of his crimes, in a single day he was again allowed to pass in and out of the innermost chambers and serve in the ancestral temple—this heavily offends the anger of spirits and men, lays anew the source of calamity and disorder, and leaves high and low bewildered and great and small gnashing their teeth."
translations.idiomatic: "Who could have expected that what had melted away would congeal again, that what had thawed would suddenly reunite? Once he regained his freedom, he at once plotted his return; with the dregs of his crimes still upon him, in a single day he was again allowed to pass in and out of the innermost chambers and serve in the ancestral temple—this heavily offends spirits and men alike, lays anew the source of calamity and disorder, and leaves court and country bewildered while all gnash their teeth."

sentences.zh: 而陛下方為之辨明，大臣方與之和解，臣竊重傷此過計也。

translations.literal: "Yet Your Majesty is now making explanations on his behalf, and great ministers are reconciling with him—I deeply grieve this excessive calculation."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet Your Majesty is now making explanations on his behalf, and great ministers are reconciling with him—I deeply grieve this misguided calculation."

sentences.zh: 自古小人復出，其害必慘，將逞其憤怨，嘯其儔伍，顛倒宇宙，陛下之威神有時而不得以自行，甚可畏也。

translations.literal: "From antiquity, when petty men return to power their harm is sure to be dire: they will vent their resentful rage, rally their kind, overturn heaven and earth, and there will be times when Your Majesty's august authority cannot be exercised at will—this is greatly to be feared."
translations.idiomatic: "From antiquity, when petty men return to power their harm is sure to be dire: they vent their resentful rage, rally their kind, overturn heaven and earth, and there are times when Your Majesty's august authority cannot be exercised at will—this is greatly to be feared."

sentences.zh: 乞休致，擢太常少卿，太子以書勉留。

translations.literal: He requested retirement; he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and the crown prince wrote urging him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement; the court promoted him to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and the crown prince wrote urging him to stay.

sentences.zh: 求補外，以秘閣修撰知福州、福建安撫，改知隆興府。

translations.literal: He sought an outside appointment and was made compiler at the Secret Repository while serving as prefect of Fuzhou and pacification commissioner of Fujian, then transferred to prefect of Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking an outside appointment, he was made compiler at the Secret Repository while serving as prefect of Fuzhou and pacification commissioner of Fujian, then transferred to prefect of Longxing.

sentences.zh: 度宗即位，召奏事，授太常少卿兼國史院編修官、實錄院檢討官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Duzong acceded, Han was summoned to report on affairs and was appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while also compiler in the National History Institute and reviser in the Veritable Records Institute.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Duzong acceded, Han was summoned to report on affairs and appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while also serving as compiler in the National History Institute and reviser in the Veritable Records Institute.

sentences.zh: 遷起居郎兼侍讀，入奏，言：“願陛下持一敬心以正百度，則追養繼孝，所以報先帝者，必益致其隆，先意承誌，所以事太母者，必益致其謹。

translations.literal: Transferred to attendant of the emperor while also reader, he entered court and said, "I wish Your Majesty would uphold a single reverent heart to set right the hundred offices—then in pursuing nurture and continuing filial piety, whereby you repay the late emperor, you will surely bring it to greater loftiness; in anticipating intent and carrying out his will, whereby you serve the empress dowager, you will surely bring it to greater care."
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to attendant of the emperor while also reader, he entered court and said: "I pray Your Majesty will uphold a single reverent heart to set right the hundred offices—then in pursuing nurture and continuing filial piety, whereby you repay the late emperor, you will surely bring it to greater loftiness; in anticipating his intent and carrying out his will, whereby you serve the empress dowager, you will surely bring it to greater care."

sentences.zh: 其愛身也，必不以物欲撓其和平；

translations.literal: "In cherishing the person, you must not let material desires disturb your peace;
translations.idiomatic: "In caring for your person, you must not let material desires disturb your peace;

sentences.zh: 其正家也，必不以私昵隳其法度。

translations.literal: in rectifying the family, you must not let private favor destroy your laws and standards."
translations.idiomatic: in rectifying the household, you must not let private favor destroy your laws and standards."

sentences.zh: 政事必出於朝廷，而預防於多門，人才必由於明揚，而深杜於邪徑。

translations.literal: "State affairs must issue from the court, with precaution taken against many gates; talent must come through open recommendation, with evil bypaths deeply blocked."
translations.idiomatic: "State affairs must issue from the court, with precaution taken against many back doors; talent must come through open recommendation, with evil bypaths deeply blocked."

sentences.zh: 兼權中書舍人，權兵部侍郎，升兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰兼直學士。

translations.literal: Concurrently acting as drafter in the Secretariat and acting vice minister of War, he was promoted to concurrent co-compiler of the National History and Veritable Records while also serving as academician on duty.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently served as acting drafter in the Secretariat and acting vice minister of War, then was promoted to concurrent co-compiler of the National History and Veritable Records while also serving as academician on duty.

sentences.zh: 累請致仕，授華文閣待制、知寧國府，賜金帶。

translations.literal: Repeatedly requesting retirement, he was granted attendant academician of the Huawen Pavilion and prefect of Ningguo, with a gold belt bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: After repeatedly requesting retirement, he was granted attendant academician of the Huawen Pavilion and appointment as prefect of Ningguo, with a gold belt bestowed.

sentences.zh: 久之，又召為刑部侍郎兼侍讀，以龍圖閣待制知福州，福建安撫使。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was again summoned as vice minister of Justice and reader, and as attendant academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall while serving as prefect of Fuzhou and pacification commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was again summoned as vice minister of Justice and reader, and as attendant academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall while serving as prefect of Fuzhou and pacification commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 改知太平州、權工部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Transferred to prefect of Taiping and acting minister of Works while also reader.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Taiping and acting minister of Works while also serving as reader.

sentences.zh: 以顯文閣直學士提舉玉隆宮。

translations.literal: As academician on duty of the Xianwen Pavilion he was made intendant of the Yulong Palace.
translations.idiomatic: As academician on duty of the Xianwen Pavilion he was appointed intendant of the Yulong Palace.

sentences.zh: 進華文閣學士，以端明殿學士致仕。

translations.literal: Advanced to academician of the Huawen Pavilion, he retired as academician of the Duanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Advanced to academician of the Huawen Pavilion, he retired with the rank of academician of the Duanming Hall.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 特贈正奉大夫，諡文清。

translations.literal: Specially posthumously granted Grand Master of Proper Service; posthumous title Wénqīng.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially posthumously granted Grand Master of Proper Service, with the posthumous title Wénqīng.

sentences.zh: 漢介潔有守，恬於進取，有文集六十卷。

translations.literal: Han was upright, pure, and principled, indifferent to advancement, and left a collected writings in sixty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Han was upright, pure, and principled, indifferent to advancement, and left collected writings in sixty juan.

sentences.zh: 何基，字子恭，婺州金華人。

translations.literal: He Ji, styled Zigong, was a native of Jinhua in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Ji, courtesy name Zigong, came from Jinhua in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父伯熭為臨川縣丞，而黃幹適知其縣事，伯熭見二子而師事焉。

translations.literal: His father Bo Chi served as assistant magistrate of Linchuan; Huang Gan happened to be administering that county, and Bo Chi, seeing his two sons, took Gan as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bo Chi served as assistant magistrate of Linchuan; Huang Gan happened to be administering that county, and when Bo Chi saw his two sons' talent, he had them take Gan as their teacher.

sentences.zh: 幹告以必有真實心地、刻苦工夫而後可，基悚惕受命。

translations.literal: Gan told them that only with a true and genuine mind-ground and painstaking effort could one succeed; Ji received the charge in fearful reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Gan told them that only with a genuine mind-ground and painstaking effort could one succeed; Ji received the charge in fearful reverence.

sentences.zh: 於是隨事誘掖，得聞淵源之懿。

translations.literal: Thereupon, guiding him in every matter, Gan enabled him to hear the profound excellence of the source-tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Gan guided him in every matter, enabling him to grasp the profound excellence of the master's teaching.

sentences.zh: 微辭奧義，研精覃思，平心易氣，以俟其通，未嚐參以己意，立異以為高，徇人而少變也。

translations.literal: In subtle words and abstruse meanings he refined his study and deepened his thought, leveling his heart and easing his temper to await understanding; he never mixed in his own ideas, set himself apart to seem lofty, or bent to others with little change.
translations.idiomatic: In subtle words and abstruse meanings he refined his study and deepened his thought, leveling his heart and easing his temper until understanding came; he never mixed in his own ideas, set himself apart to seem lofty, or bent to others with little constancy.

sentences.zh: 凡所讀無不加標點，義顯意明，有不待論說而自見者。

translations.literal: Whatever he read he punctuated without exception; meaning appeared and intent was clear, and there were passages that needed no explication to be seen for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he read he punctuated without exception; meaning appeared and intent was clear, and there were passages that needed no commentary to reveal themselves.

sentences.zh: 朱熹門人楊與立一見推服。

translations.literal: Yang Yuli, a disciple of Zhu Xi, was won over at first sight.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuli, a disciple of Zhu Xi, was won over at first sight.

sentences.zh: 來學者眾，嚐謂：“為學立誌貴堅，規模貴大，充踐服行，死而後已。

translations.literal: Students who came to study were many; he once said, "In learning, establishing one's resolve should be firm and one's scope should be great; fill out practice and carry it out in service—only after death does one stop."
translations.idiomatic: Many students came to study with him; he once said, "In learning, one's resolve must be firm and one's scope must be great; one must fill out practice and carry it through in service—only death brings an end."

sentences.zh: 讀《詩》之法，須掃蕩胸次淨盡，然後吟哦上下，諷詠從容，使人感發，方為有功。

translations.literal: "The method of reading the 《Odes》 is to sweep the breast clean to the last speck; only then chant up and down, recite with ease, and move others to feeling—only then is there achievement."
translations.idiomatic: "The method of reading the 《Odes》 is to sweep the breast utterly clean; only then may one chant up and down, recite with ease, and move others to feeling—only then has one achieved something."

sentences.zh: ”謂：“以《洪範》參之《大學》、《中庸》，有不約而符者。

translations.literal: " He said, "When the 《Great Plan》 is compared with the 《Great Learning》 and the 《Doctrine of the Mean》, there are correspondences without being forced."
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "When the 《Great Plan》 is compared with the 《Great Learning》 and the 《Doctrine of the Mean》, there are correspondences that need no forcing."

sentences.zh: ”謂：“讀《易》者，當盡去其膠固支離之見，以潔淨其心，玩精微之理，沉潛涵泳，得其根源，乃可漸觀爻象。

translations.literal: " He said, "One who reads the 《Changes》 should wholly cast off rigid, fragmented views, purify the heart, savor subtle principle, sink and immerse and bathe in it, attain its root source—only then may one gradually contemplate the line statements."
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "One who reads the 《Changes》 should wholly cast off rigid, fragmented views, purify the heart, savor subtle principle, and sink into it with deep immersion until one attains its root source—only then may one gradually contemplate the line statements."

sentences.zh: ”蓋其確守師訓，故能精義造約。

translations.literal: " This was because he faithfully kept his teacher's instruction and therefore could refine meaning and arrive at essentials.
translations.idiomatic: " This was because he faithfully kept his teacher's instruction and therefore could refine meaning and arrive at essentials.

sentences.zh: 王柏既執贄為弟子，基謙抑不以師道自尊。

translations.literal: When Wang Bai had presented his gift and become a disciple, Ji was modest and did not hold himself high in the teacher's role.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Bai had presented his gift and become a disciple, Ji was modest and did not hold himself high in the teacher's role.

sentences.zh: 柏高明絕識，序正諸經，弘論英辨，質問難疑，或一事至十往返，基終不變以待其定。

translations.literal: Bai was lofty in brilliance and unmatched in insight; he ordered and rectified the classics, offered grand discourse and eloquent disputation, and questioned and raised doubts—sometimes on a single matter there would be ten exchanges back and forth, yet Ji never changed and waited for the matter to settle.
translations.idiomatic: Bai was lofty in brilliance and unmatched in insight; he ordered and rectified the classics, offered grand discourse and eloquent disputation, and questioned and raised doubts—sometimes on a single matter there would be ten exchanges back and forth, yet Ji never shifted his ground and waited for the matter to settle.

sentences.zh: 嚐曰：“治經當謹守精玩，不必多起疑論。

translations.literal: He once said, "In treating the classics one should carefully keep and refine them—there is no need to raise many doubtful disputations."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "In treating the classics one should carefully keep and refine them—there is no need to raise many doubtful disputations."

sentences.zh: 有欲為後學言者，謹之又謹可也。

translations.literal: For those who wish to speak to later students, being cautious again and again will do.
translations.idiomatic: For those who wish to instruct later students, the utmost caution is required.

sentences.zh: ”基淳固篤實，絕類漢儒。

translations.literal: " Ji was pure, solid, and sincere, utterly resembling Han-dynasty Ru scholars.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji was pure, steadfast, and sincere, in every way resembling the Ru scholars of the Han.

sentences.zh: 雖一本於熹，然就其言發明，則精義新意愈出不窮。

translations.literal: Although he took Zhu Xi as his single root, yet in elucidating through his words, refined meanings and fresh insights issued forth without end.
translations.idiomatic: Although he took Zhu Xi as his foundation, in elucidating his teachings he produced refined meanings and fresh insights without end.

sentences.zh: 基文集三十卷，而與柏問辨者十八卷。

translations.literal: Ji's collected writings were thirty juan, and his question-and-debate exchanges with Bai were eighteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings in thirty juan, and eighteen juan of question-and-debate exchanges with Wang Bai.

sentences.zh: 郡守趙汝騰守婺，延聘請講，辭不就。

translations.literal: When Zhao Ruteng was prefect of the commandery and administered Wuzhou, he extended an invitation and requested lectures, but Ji declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Ruteng served as prefect of Wuzhou, he invited Ji to lecture, but Ji declined.

sentences.zh: 復首薦於朝，又率名從官列薦。

translations.literal: He again took the lead in recommending Ji to the court, and also led famous attendant officials in submitting joint recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: He again took the lead in recommending Ji to the court, and also led famous attendant officials in submitting joint recommendations.

sentences.zh: 通判鄭士懿、守蔡抗、楊棟相繼以請，皆辭。

translations.literal: Vice prefect Zheng Shiyi, prefect Cai Kang, and Yang Dong in succession requested him, but he declined all.
translations.idiomatic: The vice prefect Zheng Shiyi and the prefects Cai Kang and Yang Dong in succession invited him, but he declined every offer.

sentences.zh: 景定五年，詔舉賢，特薦基與建人徐幾，同被命添差婺州學教授，兼麗澤書院山長，力辭未竟，理宗崩。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingding an edict summoned the worthy; Ji and Xu Ji of Jian were specially recommended and together received orders as specially assigned professors at the Wuzhou school while also serving as head of Lizhe Academy; he strove to decline but had not finished when Emperor Lizong died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1264 an edict summoned worthy men; Ji and Xu Ji of Jian were specially recommended and together appointed as specially assigned professors at the Wuzhou school while also serving as head of Lizhe Academy; he strove to decline but had not finished when Emperor Lizong died.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳初，授史館校勘兼崇政殿說書，屢辭，改承務郎，主管西嶽廟，終亦不受也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianchun he was appointed collator in the Historiography Institute while also lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall; he repeatedly declined, was changed to Gentleman for Palace Service, made intendant of the Western Peak Temple, and in the end likewise did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianchun he was appointed collator in the Historiography Institute and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall; he repeatedly declined, was given the rank of Gentleman for Palace Service and made intendant of the Western Peak Temple, and in the end accepted none of it.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒楊文仲請於朝，諡文定。

translations.literal: Yang Wenzhong, libationer of the Directorate of Education, requested of the court the posthumous title Wendìng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wenzhong, libationer of the Directorate of Education, petitioned the court for the posthumous title Wendìng.

sentences.zh: 所著《大學發揮》、《中庸發揮》、《大傳發揮》、《易啟蒙發揮》、《通書發揮》、《近思錄發揮》。

translations.literal: His works included Elucidations on the Great Learning, Elucidations on the Doctrine of the Mean, Elucidations on the Great Commentary, Elucidations on the Introduction to the Changes, Elucidations on the Penetrating Book, and Elucidations on Reflections on Things at Hand.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Elucidations on the Great Learning, Elucidations on the Doctrine of the Mean, Elucidations on the Great Commentary, Elucidations on the Introduction to the Changes, Elucidations on the Penetrating Book, and Elucidations on Reflections on Things at Hand.

sentences.zh: 王柏，字會之，婺州金華人。

translations.literal: Wang Bai, styled Huizhi, was a native of Jinhua in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bai, courtesy name Huizhi, came from Jinhua in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 大父崇政殿說書師愈，從楊時受《易》、《論語》，既又從朱熹、張栻、呂祖謙遊。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shiyu was lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall; he studied the Changes and the Analects under Yang Shi, and afterward also associated with Zhu Xi, Zhang Shi, and Lü Zuqian.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shiyu was lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall; he studied the Changes and the Analects under Yang Shi, and later also associated with Zhu Xi, Zhang Shi, and Lü Zuqian.

sentences.zh: 父瀚，朝奉郎、主管建昌軍仙都觀，兄弟皆及熹、祖謙之門。

translations.literal: His father Han was Gentleman for Court Audience and intendant of the Xiandu Abbey in Jianchang Circuit; the brothers all reached the gates of Zhu Xi and Zuqian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Han was Gentleman for Court Audience and intendant of the Xiandu Abbey in Jianchang Circuit; all the brothers entered the circles of Zhu Xi and Lü Zuqian.

sentences.zh: 柏少慕諸葛亮為人，自號長嘯。

translations.literal: In youth Bai admired Zhuge Liang as a man and styled himself Longxiao.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Bai admired Zhuge Liang and styled himself Longxiao, "the Long Whistler."

sentences.zh: 年逾三十，始知家學之原，捐去俗學，勇於求道。

translations.literal: Past the age of thirty he first understood the source of his family's learning, cast off vulgar studies, and was bold in seeking the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Past thirty he first grasped the source of his family's learning, cast off vulgar studies, and devoted himself boldly to seeking the Way.

sentences.zh: 與其友汪開之著《論語通旨》，至“居處恭，執事敬”，惕然歎曰：“長嘯非聖門持敬之道。

translations.literal: With his friend Wang Kaizhi he wrote Comprehensive Meaning of the Analects; when he reached "In dwelling be respectful, in handling affairs be reverent," he sighed in alarm and said, "Longxiao is not the sage school's way of upholding reverence."
translations.idiomatic: With his friend Wang Kaizhi he wrote Comprehensive Meaning of the Analects; when he reached "In dwelling be respectful, in handling affairs be reverent," he sighed in alarm and said, "Longxiao is not the sage school's way of upholding reverence."

sentences.zh: ”亟更以魯齋。

translations.literal: " He at once changed it to Luzhai.
translations.idiomatic: " He at once changed his style to Luzhai, "the Lu Studio."

sentences.zh: 從熹門人遊，或語以何基嚐從黃幹得熹之傳，即往從之，授以立誌居敬之旨，且作《魯齋箴》勉之。

translations.literal: Associating with Zhu Xi's disciples, someone told him that He Ji had once received Zhu Xi's transmission through Huang Gan; he at once went to follow Ji, who taught him the aim of establishing resolve and dwelling in reverence, and also wrote the "Admonition of the Lu Studio" to encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: While associating with Zhu Xi's disciples, he was told that He Ji had received Zhu Xi's transmission through Huang Gan; he at once went to study with Ji, who taught him to establish resolve and dwell in reverence, and wrote the "Admonition of the Lu Studio" to encourage him.

sentences.zh: 質實堅苦，有疑必從基質之。

translations.literal: Solid, sincere, firm, and painstaking, whenever he had doubts he always went to Ji to question him.
translations.idiomatic: Solid, sincere, and painstaking, whenever he had doubts he always took them to Ji for resolution.

sentences.zh: 於《論語》、《大學》、《中庸》、《孟子》、《通鑒綱目》標注點校，尤為精密。

translations.literal: In the Analects, Great Learning, Doctrine of the Mean, Mencius, and Comprehensive Mirror Outline he marked punctuation and collated the text, especially with meticulous precision.
translations.idiomatic: His punctuation and collation of the Analects, Great Learning, Doctrine of the Mean, Mencius, and Comprehensive Mirror Outline were especially meticulous.

sentences.zh: 作《敬齋箴圖》。

translations.literal: He wrote the Diagram of the Admonition of the Reverent Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Diagram of the Admonition of the Reverent Studio.

sentences.zh: 夙興見廟，治家嚴飭。

translations.literal: Rising early he visited the ancestral temple; in governing the household he was strict and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He rose early to visit the ancestral temple and governed his household with strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 當暑閉閣靜坐，子弟白事，非衣冠不見也。

translations.literal: In summer heat he closed the pavilion and sat in quiet; when sons and younger brothers reported affairs, unless in cap and gown he would not see them.
translations.idiomatic: In summer he shut himself in his study to sit in quiet; when sons and younger brothers came to report affairs, he would not receive them unless they were properly dressed.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事其伯兄甚恭。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he served his elder brother with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he served his elder brother with great respect.

sentences.zh: 季弟早喪，撫其孤，又割田予之。

translations.literal: His youngest brother died early; he nurtured the orphan and also divided fields and gave them to him.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest brother died young; he raised the orphan and also gave him a portion of the family fields.

sentences.zh: 收合宗族，周恤扶持之。

translations.literal: He gathered the clan together and supported them with comprehensive care.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the clan together and supported them with comprehensive care.

sentences.zh: 開之沒，家貧，為之斂且葬焉。

translations.literal: When Kaizhi died, his family was poor; Bai laid him out and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: When Kaizhi died in poverty, Bai laid out his body and buried him.

sentences.zh: 來學者眾，其教必先之以《大學》。

translations.literal: Students who came to study were many; in his teaching he always began with the Great Learning.
translations.idiomatic: Many students came to study with him; in his teaching he always began with the Great Learning.

sentences.zh: 蔡抗、楊棟相繼守婺，趙景緯守台，聘為麗澤、上蔡兩書院師，鄉之耆德皆執弟子禮。

translations.literal: Cai Kang and Yang Dong in succession administered Wuzhou; Zhao Jingwei administered Taizhou; they engaged him as teacher at the Lizhe and Shangcai academies, and the elders of the district all performed the rites of disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Kang and Yang Dong in succession served as prefect of Wuzhou, and Zhao Jingwei as prefect of Taizhou; they engaged him as teacher at the Lizhe and Shangcai academies, and the district elders all performed the rites of disciples before him.

sentences.zh: 理宗崩，率諸生製服臨於郡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Lizong died, he led the students in putting on mourning dress and attending at the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Lizong died, he led his students in putting on mourning dress and attending at the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 柏之言曰：“伏羲則《河圖》以畫八卦，文王推八卦以合《河圖》者，先天後天之宗祖也。

translations.literal: Bai said, "Fuxi took the River Chart to draw the Eight Trigrams; King Wen extended the Eight Trigrams to harmonize with the River Chart—these are the ancestors of the Before Heaven and After Heaven arrangements."
translations.idiomatic: Bai said, "Fuxi took the River Chart to draw the Eight Trigrams; King Wen extended the Eight Trigrams to harmonize with the River Chart—these are the ancestors of the Before Heaven and After Heaven arrangements."

sentences.zh: 《河圖》是逐位奇偶之交，後天是統體奇偶之交，惟四生數不動。

translations.literal: "The River Chart is the alternation of odd and even position by position; After Heaven is the alternation of odd and even in the whole body—only the four generating numbers do not move."
translations.idiomatic: "The River Chart alternates odd and even position by position; After Heaven alternates odd and even in the whole body—only the four generating numbers remain fixed."

sentences.zh: 以四成數而下上之，上偶下奇，莫匪自然。

translations.literal: "Taking the four completing numbers and moving them up and down, even above and odd below—none of it is not natural."
translations.idiomatic: "Taking the four completing numbers and moving them up and down, even above and odd below—all of it follows nature."

sentences.zh: ”又曰：“大禹得《洛書》而列九疇，箕子得九疇而傳《洪範》，範圍之數，不期而暗合。

translations.literal: " He also said, "Yu the Great obtained the Luo Document and arrayed the Nine Categories; Jizi obtained the Nine Categories and transmitted the Great Plan—the numbers of the Plan's scope accorded in secret without being sought."
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Yu the Great obtained the Luo Document and arrayed the Nine Categories; Jizi obtained the Nine Categories and transmitted the Great Plan—the numbers of the Plan's scope accorded in secret without being sought."

sentences.zh: 《洪範》者，經傳之宗祖乎！

translations.literal: "Is the Great Plan not the ancestor of the classics and commentaries!"
translations.idiomatic: "Is not the Great Plan the ancestor of the classics and commentaries!"

sentences.zh: ‘初一曰五行’以下六十五字為《洪範》，‘五皇極’以下六十四字為皇極經，此帝王相傳之大訓，非箕子之言也。

translations.literal: "From 'First, the Five Elements' below, sixty-five characters are the Great Plan; from 'Five, the Imperial Extreme' below, sixty-four characters are the Classic of the Imperial Extreme—this is the great instruction handed down among emperors and kings, not the words of Jizi."
translations.idiomatic: "From 'First, the Five Elements' below, sixty-five characters form the Great Plan; from 'Five, the Imperial Extreme' below, sixty-four characters form the Classic of the Imperial Extreme—this is the great instruction handed down among emperors and kings, not the words of Jizi."

sentences.zh: ”又曰：“今《詩》三百五篇，豈盡定於夫子之手？

translations.literal: " He also said, "Are the present three hundred and five pieces of the Odes all fixed by the Master's hand?"
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Are the present three hundred and five pieces of the Odes all fixed by the Master's own hand?"

sentences.zh: 所刪之詩，容或有存於閭巷浮薄之口，漢儒取於補亡。

translations.literal: "The odes he deleted may perhaps still survive in the mouths of lanes and alleys and frivolous folk; Han Ru scholars took them to fill lacunae."
translations.idiomatic: "The odes he deleted may still survive in the mouths of common folk; Han scholars took them to fill lacunae."

sentences.zh: ”乃定《二南》各十有一篇，兩兩相配。

translations.literal: " He then fixed the Two Souths at eleven pieces each, paired two by two.
translations.idiomatic: " He then fixed the Two Souths at eleven pieces each, paired two by two.

sentences.zh: 退《何彼穠矣》、《甘棠》歸之《王風》，削去《野有死麕》，黜鄭、衛淫奔之詩。

translations.literal: He demoted "How Luxuriant Those Branches" and "Sweet Pear-Tree" to the Royal Airs, cut out "In the Wilds Is a Dead Roebuck," and dismissed the licentious, runaway odes of Zheng and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He demoted "How Luxuriant Those Branches" and "Sweet Pear-Tree" to the Royal Airs, cut out "In the Wilds Is a Dead Roebuck," and dismissed the licentious odes of Zheng and Wei.

sentences.zh: 又作《春秋發揮》。

translations.literal: He also wrote Elucidations on the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Elucidations on the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 又曰：“《大學致知格物章》未嚐亡。

translations.literal: He also said, "The chapter on extending knowledge and investigating things in the Great Learning has never been lost."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The chapter on extending knowledge and investigating things in the Great Learning has never been lost."

sentences.zh: ”還《知止》章於《聽訟》之上。

translations.literal: " He restored the chapter on knowing where to stop above the chapter on hearing lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: " He restored the chapter on knowing where to stop above the chapter on hearing lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 謂“《中庸》古有二篇，誠明可為綱，不可為目。

translations.literal: He held that "anciently the Doctrine of the Mean had two sections; sincerity and clarity could serve as the guiding thread but not as a chapter heading."
translations.idiomatic: He held that "anciently the Doctrine of the Mean had two sections; sincerity and clarity could serve as the guiding thread but not as a chapter heading."

sentences.zh: ” 定《中庸》誠明各十一章，其卓識獨見多此類也。

translations.literal: " He fixed the sincerity-and-clarity sections of the Doctrine of the Mean at eleven chapters each; his outstanding insight and singular views were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: " He fixed the sincerity-and-clarity sections of the Doctrine of the Mean at eleven chapters each; his outstanding insight and singular views were mostly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 其卒，整衣冠端坐，揮婦人勿近。

translations.literal: At his death he straightened cap and gown and sat upright, waving women not to approach.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he straightened his cap and gown and sat upright, waving the women away.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒楊文仲請於朝，諡曰文憲。

translations.literal: Yang Wenzhong, libationer of the Directorate of Education, requested of the court the posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wenzhong, libationer of the Directorate of Education, petitioned the court for the posthumous title Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 所著有《讀易記》、《涵古易說》、《大象衍義》、《涵古圖書》、《讀書記》、《書疑》、《詩辨說》、《讀春秋記》、《論語衍義》、《太極衍義》、《伊洛精義》、《研幾圖》、《魯經章句》、《論語通旨》、《孟子通旨》、《書附傳》、《左氏正傳》、《續國語》、《閫學之書》、《文章復古》、《文章續古》、《濂洛文統》、《擬道學志》、《朱子指要》、《詩可言》、《天文考》、《地理考》、《墨林考》、《大爾雅》、《六義字原》、《正始之音》、《帝王曆數》、《江左淵源》、《伊洛精義雜志》、《周子》、《發遣三昧》、《文章指南》、《朝華集》、《紫陽詩類》、《家乘》、文集。

translations.literal: His works included Records of Reading the Changes, Comprehensive Ancient Explanations of the Changes, Extended Meaning of the Great Images, Comprehensive Ancient Diagrams and Writings, Records of Reading, Doubts on the Documents, Discriminating Explanations on the Odes, Records of Reading the Spring and Autumn, Extended Meaning of the Analects, Extended Meaning of the Supreme Polarity, Essential Meaning of the Yi-Luo School, Diagram of Investigating the Subtle, Chapter and Sentence Commentary on the Lu Classics, Comprehensive Meaning of the Analects, Comprehensive Meaning of Mencius, Attached Commentary on the Documents, Corrected Tradition of Mr. Zuo, Continuation of the Discourses of the States, Writings on Inner Learning, Restoration of Ancient Style in Literature, Continuation of Ancient Style in Literature, Literary Tradition of Lian and Luo, Draft Record of the Way Learning, Essentials of Master Zhu, The Odes May Be Spoken, Examination of Astronomy, Examination of Geography, Examination of the Ink Forest, Great Erya, Original Characters of the Six Principles, Sounds of the Correct Beginning, Imperial Chronology, Sources of the Jiang Left, Miscellaneous Records of Yi-Luo Essentials, Master Zhou, Dispelling the Threefold Samadhi, Guide to Literature, Collection of Morning Splendor, Zhu Xi's Ode Categories, Family Registers, and collected writings.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Records of Reading the Changes, Comprehensive Ancient Explanations of the Changes, Extended Meaning of the Great Images, Comprehensive Ancient Diagrams and Writings, Records of Reading, Doubts on the Documents, Discriminating Explanations on the Odes, Records of Reading the Spring and Autumn, Extended Meaning of the Analects, Extended Meaning of the Supreme Polarity, Essential Meaning of the Yi-Luo School, Diagram of Investigating the Subtle, Chapter and Sentence Commentary on the Lu Classics, Comprehensive Meaning of the Analects and Mencius, Attached Commentary on the Documents, Corrected Tradition of Mr. Zuo, Continuation of the Discourses of the States, Writings on Inner Learning, Restoration and Continuation of Ancient Style in Literature, Literary Tradition of Lian and Luo, Draft Record of the Way Learning, Essentials of Master Zhu, The Odes May Be Spoken, examinations of astronomy, geography, and the ink forest, Great Erya, Original Characters of the Six Principles, Sounds of the Correct Beginning, Imperial Chronology, Sources of the Jiang Left, Miscellaneous Records of Yi-Luo Essentials, Master Zhou, Dispelling the Threefold Samadhi, Guide to Literature, Collection of Morning Splendor, Zhu Xi's Ode Categories, family registers, and collected writings.

sentences.zh: 徐夢莘字商老，臨江人。

translations.literal: Xu Mengshen, styled Shanglao, was a native of Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mengshen, courtesy name Shanglao, came from Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 幼慧，耽嗜經史，下至稗官小說，寓目成誦。

translations.literal: Clever in youth, he was addicted to the classics and histories, down to unofficial histories and minor tales—what met his eye he could recite.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from childhood, he devoured the classics and histories, even unofficial histories and minor tales—whatever met his eye he could recite from memory.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十四年舉進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Shaoxing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1154 he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 曆官為南安軍教授。

translations.literal: Through offices he served as professor of Nan'an Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served as professor of Nan'an Circuit.

sentences.zh: 改知湘陰縣。

translations.literal: Transferred to magistrate of Xiangyin County.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Xiangyin County.

sentences.zh: 會湖南帥括田，號增耕稅，他邑奉令惟謹。

translations.literal: When the Hunan commander surveyed fields and called it increasing cultivated land tax, other counties obeyed the order with utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hunan commander surveyed fields under the banner of increasing cultivated-land tax, other counties obeyed with utmost care.

sentences.zh: 夢莘獨謂邑無新田，租稅無從出。

translations.literal: Mengshen alone said the county had no new fields and rent and tax had nowhere to come from.
translations.idiomatic: Mengshen alone protested that the county had no new fields and that rent and tax could not be produced from nothing.

sentences.zh: 帥恚其私於民，欲從簿書間攈摭其過，終莫能得，由是反器重之。

translations.literal: The commander resented his favoring the people and wished to pick out faults from the account books, but in the end could obtain none; because of this he instead came to value him highly.
translations.idiomatic: The commander resented his siding with the people and tried to find fault in the account books, but could discover none; he therefore came to value him all the more.

sentences.zh: 尋主管廣西轉運司文字。

translations.literal: Soon he was made in charge of documents for the Guangxi Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was placed in charge of documents for the Guangxi Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷議易二廣鹽法，遣廣西安撫司幹官胡廷直與東西漕臣集議於境。

translations.literal: At the time the court debated changing the salt law of the Two Guangs and sent Hu Tingzhi, staff officer of the Guangxi Pacification Commission, to meet with the transport officials of east and west at the border for joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court debated changing the salt law of the Two Guangs and sent Hu Tingzhi, staff officer of the Guangxi Pacification Commission, to meet with the eastern and western transport officials at the border for joint deliberation.

sentences.zh: 夢莘從行，謂：“廣西阻山，止當仍官般法，則害不及民。

translations.literal: Mengshen accompanied the mission and said, "Guangxi is blocked by mountains and should only continue the official transport method—then harm will not reach the people."
translations.idiomatic: Mengshen accompanied the mission and argued, "Guangxi is hemmed in by mountains and should keep the official transport method—only then will the people be spared harm."

sentences.zh: 廣東諸郡並江，或可容客販，未宜遽以二廣概行。

translations.literal: "The prefectures of Guangdong all border the rivers and might permit merchant transport; it is not fitting to apply the Two Guangs uniformly at once."
translations.idiomatic: "The prefectures of Guangdong all border the rivers and might permit merchant transport; it is not fitting to apply one policy to both Guangs at once."

sentences.zh: ”議與廷直不合。

translations.literal: " His views did not accord with Tingzhi's.
translations.idiomatic: " His views did not accord with Hu Tingzhi's.

sentences.zh: 廷直竟遂其說，以客販變法得為轉運使。

translations.literal: Tingzhi in the end carried out his own plan; through the merchant-transport reform he became transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Tingzhi in the end carried out his own plan and, through the merchant-transport reform, became transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 夢莘既知賓州，猶以前議為梗法，罷去。

translations.literal: After Mengshen became prefect of Binzhou, he was still dismissed because his earlier views were deemed to obstruct the law.
translations.idiomatic: After Mengshen became prefect of Binzhou, he was dismissed because his earlier opposition was deemed to obstruct the new law.

sentences.zh: 不三年，二廣商賈毀業，民苦無鹽，復從官般法矣。

translations.literal: Within three years merchants in the Two Guangs were ruined in their trades, the people suffered from lack of salt, and the official transport method was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years merchants in the Two Guangs were ruined, the people suffered from lack of salt, and the official transport method was restored.

sentences.zh: 夢莘恬於榮進，每念生於靖康之亂，四歲而江西阻訌，母繈負亡去得免。

translations.literal: Mengshen was indifferent to glory and advancement; he often recalled that he was born amid the disorders of the Jingkang era, and at four years old, when Jiangxi was cut off by rebellion, his mother carried him on her back and fled, and thus he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Mengshen was indifferent to glory and advancement; he often recalled that he was born amid the disorders of the Jingkang era, and that at four, when Jiangxi was cut off by rebellion, his mother carried him on her back and fled to safety.

sentences.zh: 思究見顛末，乃網羅舊聞，會稡同異，為《三朝北盟會編》二百五十卷，自政和七年海上之盟，訖紹興三十一年完顏亮之斃，上下四十五年，凡曰敕、曰製、誥、詔、國書、書疏、奏議、記序、碑誌，登載靡遺。

translations.literal: Wishing to investigate beginnings and ends, he gathered old reports, assembled agreements and differences, and compiled the Collected Records of Northern Alliances across Three Reigns in 250 juan—from the maritime alliance of the seventh year of Zhenghe to the death of Wanyan Liang in the thirty-first year of Shaoxing, forty-five years in all; whatever were called edicts, regulations, patent letters, proclamations, state letters, letters and memorials, memorials and deliberations, records and prefaces, steles and epitaphs—none were omitted from registration.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to trace events from beginning to end, he gathered old reports and assembled agreements and differences into the Collected Records of Northern Alliances across Three Reigns in 250 juan—from the maritime alliance of 1117 to the death of Wanyan Liang in 1161, forty-five years in all; edicts, regulations, patent letters, proclamations, state letters, memorials, deliberations, records, prefaces, steles, and epitaphs were all included without omission.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而嘉之，擢直秘閣。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and commended him, promoting him to directorship of the Secret Repository.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it and commended him, promoting him to directorship of the Secret Repository.

sentences.zh: 夢莘平生多所著，有《集補》，有《會錄》，有《讀書記志》，有《集醫錄》，有《集仙錄》，皆以“儒榮”冠之。

translations.literal: Throughout his life Mengshen wrote many works: there were Collected Supplements, Collected Records, Records of Reading Notes, Collected Medical Records, and Collected Immortal Records—all prefixed with "Ru Glory."
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life Mengshen wrote many works, including Collected Supplements, Collected Records, Records of Reading Notes, Collected Medical Records, and Collected Immortal Records—all prefixed with "Ru Glory."

sentences.zh: 其嗜學博文，蓋孜孜焉死而後已者。

translations.literal: His love of learning and breadth of culture were surely the tireless pursuit that ends only after death.
translations.idiomatic: His love of learning and breadth of culture were a tireless pursuit that ended only with his death.

sentences.zh: 開禧元年秋八月卒，年八十二。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn of the first year of Kaixi he died at the age of eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of 1205 he died at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 夢莘弟得之，從子天麟。

translations.literal: Mengshen's younger brother was Dezhi; his nephew was Tianlin.
translations.idiomatic: Mengshen's younger brother was Dezhi; his nephew was Tianlin.

sentences.zh: 得之字思叔，淳熙十年舉進士。

translations.literal: Dezhi, styled Sishu, passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of Chunxi.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhi, courtesy name Sishu, passed the jinshi examination in 1183.

sentences.zh: 部使者以廉吏薦，以通直郎致仕。

translations.literal: A ministry envoy recommended him as an incorrupt official; he retired as Gentleman for Direct Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: A ministry envoy recommended him as an incorrupt official; he retired with the rank of Gentleman for Direct Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 安貧樂分，不貪不躁，著《左氏國紀》、《史記年紀》作《具敝篋筆略》、《鼓吹詞》、《郴江志》。

translations.literal: Content with poverty and delighting in his lot, neither greedy nor restless, he wrote Mr. Zuo's Chronicle of States, Annals of the Records of the Historian, Brief Notes of the Worn Writing Case, Songs of the Processional Drums, and Gazetteer of the Chen River.
translations.idiomatic: Content with poverty and delighting in his lot, neither greedy nor restless, he wrote Mr. Zuo's Chronicle of States, Annals of the Records of the Historian, Brief Notes of the Worn Writing Case, Songs of the Processional Drums, and Gazetteer of the Chen River.

sentences.zh: 天麟字仲祥，開禧元年進士。

translations.literal: Tianlin, styled Zhongxiang, was a jinshi graduate of the first year of Kaixi.
translations.idiomatic: Tianlin, courtesy name Zhongxiang, was a jinshi graduate of 1205.

sentences.zh: 調撫州教授，曆湖廣總領所幹辦公事、臨安府教授、浙西提舉常平司幹官、主管禮兵部架閣、宗學諭、武學博士。

translations.literal: Assigned professor of Fuzhou, he served successively as staff officer of the Huguang General Comptroller's Office, professor of Lin'an, staff officer of the Zhexi Ever-Normal Granaries, director of the Ministry of Rites and War archives, instructor at the Imperial Clan Academy, and erudite of the Military Studies Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned professor of Fuzhou, he served successively as staff officer of the Huguang General Comptroller's Office, professor of Lin'an, staff officer of the Zhexi Ever-Normal Granaries, director of the Ministry of Rites and War archives, instructor at the Imperial Clan Academy, and erudite of the Military Studies Academy.

sentences.zh: 輪對，言人主當持心以敬。

translations.literal: In a rotating audience he said the ruler should uphold the heart with reverence.
translations.idiomatic: In a rotating audience he said the ruler should uphold his heart in reverence.

sentences.zh: 奉祠仙都觀，通判惠、潭二州，權英德府，權發遣廣西轉運判官。

translations.literal: He received temple service at the Xiandu Abbey, served as vice prefect of Hui and Tan prefectures, acting prefect of Yingde, and acting dispatched transport judge of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He received temple service at the Xiandu Abbey, served as vice prefect of Hui and Tan, acting prefect of Yingde, and acting dispatched transport judge of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 所至興學明教，有惠政。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he promoted schools and clarified teaching, and had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he promoted schools and clarified teaching, and his administration was benevolent.

sentences.zh: 著《西漢會要》七十卷、《東漢會要》四十卷、《漢兵本末》一卷、《西漢地理疏》六卷、《山經》三十卷。

translations.literal: He wrote Essentials of the Western Han in seventy juan, Essentials of the Eastern Han in forty juan, Origins and Ends of Han Military Affairs in one juan, Exegesis on Western Han Geography in six juan, and Classic of Mountains in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Essentials of the Western Han in seventy juan, Essentials of the Eastern Han in forty juan, Origins and Ends of Han Military Affairs in one juan, Exegesis on Western Han Geography in six juan, and Classic of Mountains in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 既謝官，作亭蕭灘之上，畫嚴子陵像而事之。

translations.literal: After resigning office he built a pavilion above Xiaotan, painted an image of Yan Ziling, and served it.
translations.idiomatic: After resigning office he built a pavilion above Xiaotan, painted an image of Yan Ziling, and venerated it.

sentences.zh: 李心傳，字微之，宗正寺簿舜臣之子也。

translations.literal: Li Xinchuan, styled Weizhi, was the son of Shunchen, registrar of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xinchuan, courtesy name Weizhi, was the son of Shunchen, registrar of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 慶元元年薦於鄉，既下第，絕意不復應舉，閉戶著書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingyuan he was recommended in the district; after failing the examination he resolved never to compete again and shut his door to write books.
translations.idiomatic: In 1195 he was recommended in the district examination; after failing, he resolved never to compete again and shut his door to write.

sentences.zh: 晚因崔與之、許奕、魏了翁等合前後二十三人之薦，自製置司敦遣至闕下。

translations.literal: Late in life, through the combined recommendations of twenty-three men before and after, including Cui Yuzhi, Xu Yi, and Wei Liaoweng, he was earnestly sent from the pacification commission to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life, through the combined recommendations of twenty-three men including Cui Yuzhi, Xu Yi, and Wei Liaoweng, the pacification commission earnestly sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 為史館校勘，賜進士出身，專修《中興四朝帝紀》。

translations.literal: He became collator in the Historiography Institute, was granted jinshi status, and specialized in compiling the Imperial Annals of the Four Reigns of the Restoration.
translations.idiomatic: He became collator in the Historiography Institute, was granted jinshi status, and specialized in compiling the Imperial Annals of the Four Reigns of the Restoration.

sentences.zh: 甫成其三，因言者罷，添差通判成都府。

translations.literal: When he had just completed three of them, because of critics he was dismissed and made specially assigned vice prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When he had just completed three of them, critics brought about his dismissal and he was made specially assigned vice prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 尋遷著作佐郎，兼四川製置司參議官。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to assistant in the Composition Office while also serving as deliberator on the Sichuan Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to assistant in the Composition Office while also serving as deliberator on the Sichuan Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 詔無入議幕，許辟官置局，踵修《十三朝會要》。

translations.literal: An edict forbade him to enter the deliberation staff but permitted him to recruit officials and establish a bureau to continue compiling the Essentials of Thirteen Reigns.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forbade him to enter the deliberation staff but permitted him to recruit officials and establish a bureau to continue compiling the Essentials of Thirteen Reigns.

sentences.zh: 端平三年成書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Duanping the book was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1236 the work was completed.

sentences.zh: 召赴闕，為工部侍郎，言：

translations.literal: Summoned to the capital, he became vice minister of Works and said:
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the capital, he became vice minister of Works and said:

sentences.zh: 臣聞“大兵之後，必有凶年”。

translations.literal: "Your subject has heard that 'after great warfare there is sure to be a year of famine.'"
translations.idiomatic: "Your subject has heard that 'after great warfare there is sure to be a year of famine.'"

sentences.zh: 蓋其殺戮之多，賦斂之重，使斯民怨怒之氣，上幹陰陽之和，至於此極也。

translations.literal: This is because the killing was so great and the levies so heavy that the resentful rage of the people offended the harmony of yin and yang, reaching this extreme.
translations.idiomatic: This is because the killing was so great and the levies so heavy that the people's resentful rage offended the harmony of yin and yang, reaching this extreme.

sentences.zh: 陛下所宜與諸大臣掃除亂政，與民更始，以為消惡運、迎善祥之計。

translations.literal: What Your Majesty should do with the great ministers is sweep away disorderly government and make a fresh start with the people, as a plan to dispel evil fortune and welcome good omens.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should join with the great ministers to sweep away disorderly government and make a fresh start with the people, as a plan to dispel evil fortune and welcome good omens.

sentences.zh: 而法弊未嚐更張，民勞不加振德，既無能改於其舊，而殆有甚焉。

translations.literal: Yet defective laws have never been reformed, the people's toil has not been relieved with restorative virtue—unable to change the old, things have almost grown worse.
translations.idiomatic: Yet defective laws have never been reformed and the people's toil has not been relieved—unable to change the old ways, things have almost grown worse.

sentences.zh: 故帝德未至於罔愆，朝綱或苦於多紊，廉平之吏，所在鮮見，而貪利無恥，敢於為惡之人，挾敵興兵，四面而起，以求逞其所欲。

translations.literal: Therefore imperial virtue has not reached freedom from fault, court standards sometimes suffer from much disorder, incorrupt and fair officials are rarely seen anywhere, while the greedy and shameless who dare do evil, taking advantage of enemies to raise troops, rise on every side to satisfy their desires.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore imperial virtue has not reached freedom from fault, court standards are often in disorder, incorrupt officials are rarely seen, while greedy, shameless men who dare do evil, taking advantage of enemies to raise troops, rise on every side to satisfy their desires.

sentences.zh: 如此而望五福來備，百穀用成，是緣木而求魚也。

translations.literal: To hope in such circumstances that the five blessings will all arrive and the hundred grains be brought to completion is to climb a tree to seek fish.
translations.idiomatic: To hope in such circumstances that the five blessings will all arrive and the hundred grains flourish is to climb a tree to catch fish.

sentences.zh: 臣考致旱之由，曰和糴增多而民怨，曰流散無所歸而民怨，曰檢稅不盡實而民怨，曰籍貲不以罪而民怨。

translations.literal: Your subject examines the causes of drought: he says harmonized purchase has increased and the people resent it; he says the displaced have nowhere to return and the people resent it; he says tax inspection is not fully truthful and the people resent it; he says asset registration is not based on crime and the people resent it.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject examines the causes of drought: harmonized purchase has increased and the people resent it; the displaced have nowhere to return and the people resent it; tax inspection is not truthful and the people resent it; asset registration punishes without crime and the people resent it.

sentences.zh: 凡此皆起於大兵之後，而勢未有以消之，故愈積而愈極也。

translations.literal: All these arose after great warfare, and the momentum has had no means of being dispelled, so they accumulate ever more extremely.
translations.idiomatic: All these arose after great warfare, and nothing has dispelled their momentum, so they accumulate ever more extremely.

sentences.zh: 成湯聖主也，而桑林之禱，猶以六事自責。

translations.literal: Emperor Tang was a sage ruler, yet in his prayer at the Mulberry Grove he still blamed himself on six matters.
translations.idiomatic: Even Emperor Tang, a sage ruler, still took blame upon himself for six failings in his prayer at the Mulberry Grove.

sentences.zh: 陛下願治，七年於此，災祥饑饉，史不絕書，其故何哉？

translations.literal: Your Majesty desires good governance, and seven years have passed to this point—omens, disasters, and famine fill the histories without cease. What is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has long desired good governance, yet for seven years now omens, disasters, and famine have filled the histories without end. What is the cause?

sentences.zh: 朝令夕改，靡有常規，則政不節矣；

translations.literal: Orders issued in the morning are changed by evening, with nothing fixed as standard—then government lacks restraint;
translations.idiomatic: When orders change from morning to evening and nothing holds steady, government loses discipline;

sentences.zh: 行齎居送，略無罷日，則使民疾矣；

translations.literal: Those who travel bearing provisions and those who stay to send them off have scarcely a day of rest—then the people are exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: When travelers and those who see them off have scarcely a day free of corvée, the people are worn to exhaustion;

sentences.zh: 陪都園廟，工作甚殷，則土木營矣；

translations.literal: At the secondary capital, gardens and temples have work extremely pressing—then earth-and-wood construction flourishes;
