translations.idiomatic: When gardens and temples at the secondary capital demand ceaseless labor, building projects run rampant;

sentences.zh: 潛邸女冠，聲焰茲熾，則女謁盛矣；

translations.literal: Taoist nuns from the prince's former residence have influence blazing bright—then female intercessors abound;
translations.idiomatic: When Taoist nuns from the prince's old residence wield ever greater influence, female go-betweens at court multiply;

sentences.zh: 珍玩之獻，罕聞卻絕，則包苴行矣；

translations.literal: Rarely is heard the rejection of gifts of precious curios—then wrapped bribes flourish;
translations.idiomatic: When gifts of rare treasures are scarcely ever refused, bribery becomes routine;

sentences.zh: 鯁切之言，類多厭棄，則讒夫昌矣。

translations.literal: Blunt and earnest words are mostly despised and cast aside—then slanderers prosper.
translations.idiomatic: When blunt, earnest remonstrance is mostly scorned and rejected, flatterers and slanderers thrive.

sentences.zh: 此六事者一或有焉，猶足以致旱。

translations.literal: If even one of these six matters exists, it is still enough to bring drought.
translations.idiomatic: If even one of these six faults is present, it is enough to cause drought.

sentences.zh: 願亟降罪己之詔，修六事以回天心。

translations.literal: I pray that you hasten to issue a self-reproach edict and rectify these six matters to turn back Heaven's mind.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty will quickly issue an edict of self-reproach and rectify these six matters to win back Heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 群臣之中有獻聚斂剽竊之論以求進者，必重黜之，俾不得以上誣聖德，則旱雖烈，猶可弭也。

translations.literal: Among the ministers, any who advance proposals for aggregation, plunder, and extortion to seek promotion must be severely dismissed, so they cannot deceive your sacred virtue above—then even if the drought is severe, it can still be quelled.
translations.idiomatic: Any minister who urges schemes of extortion and plunder to win advancement must be severely dismissed, so that none may mislead Your Majesty's sacred virtue from above; then even a fierce drought may yet be stilled.

sentences.zh: 然民怨於內，敵逼於外，事窮勢迫，何所不至！

translations.literal: Yet the people resent within, enemies press from without, affairs reach their limit and momentum is forced—what will not happen!
translations.idiomatic: Yet with the people resentful within and enemies pressing from without, when affairs reach their limit and pressure mounts, what calamity may not follow!

sentences.zh: 陛下雖謀臣如雲，猛將如雨，亦不知所以為策矣。

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty has scheming ministers thick as clouds and fierce generals dense as rain, you still will not know what policy to adopt.
translations.idiomatic: Even with scheming ministers thick as clouds and fierce generals dense as rain, Your Majesty will still not know what course to take.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復以言去，奉祠居潮州。

translations.literal: Before long, he was again dismissed for his words and took a temple stipend, residing in Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again dismissed for his remonstrance, took a temple stipend, and lived in Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 淳祐元年罷祠，復予，又罷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunyou his temple stipend was revoked, then restored, then revoked again.
translations.idiomatic: In 1241 his temple stipend was revoked, then restored, and then revoked once more.

sentences.zh: 三年，致仕，卒，年七十有八。

translations.literal: In the third year he retired from office, then died at the age of seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he retired, then died at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 心傳有史才，通故實，然其作吳獵、項安世傳，褒貶有愧秉筆之旨。

translations.literal: Xinchuan had talent for history and mastered old facts, yet in his biographies of Wu Lie and Xiang Anshi, his praise and blame fell short of the historian's duty.
translations.idiomatic: Xinchuan had a historian's talent and mastered the facts of the past, yet in his biographies of Wu Lie and Xiang Anshi his judgments fell short of the historian's charge.

sentences.zh: 蓋其誌常重川蜀，而薄東南之士雲。

translations.literal: This was because his intent always valued the Shu region and slighted the scholars of the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: For his mind always favored Sichuan and looked down on scholars of the southeast.

sentences.zh: 所著成書，有《高宗係年錄》二百卷、《學易編》五卷、《誦詩訓》五卷、《春秋考》十三卷、《禮辨》二十三卷、《讀史考》十二卷、《舊聞證誤》十五卷、《朝野雜記》四十卷、《道命錄》五卷、《西陲泰定錄》九十卷、《辨南遷錄》一卷、詩文一百卷。

translations.literal: Completed books he authored included the "Chronological Record of Emperor Gaozong" in two hundred juan, "Compilation on Learning the Changes" in five juan, "Instructions for Reciting the Odes" in five juan, "Examination of the Spring and Autumn Annals" in thirteen juan, "Discriminations on Ritual" in twenty-three juan, "Examination in Reading History" in twelve juan, "Verification of Errors in Old Reports" in fifteen juan, "Miscellaneous Records of Court and Countryside" in forty juan, "Record of the Way and Fate" in five juan, "Record of Pacification on the Western Frontier" in ninety juan, "Correction of the Record of the Southern Migration" in one juan, and collected poems and prose in one hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: His completed works included the "Chronological Record of Emperor Gaozong" (200 juan), "Compilation on Learning the Changes" (5 juan), "Instructions for Reciting the Odes" (5 juan), "Examination of the Spring and Autumn Annals" (13 juan), "Discriminations on Ritual" (23 juan), "Examination in Reading History" (12 juan), "Verification of Errors in Old Reports" (15 juan), "Miscellaneous Records of Court and Countryside" (40 juan), "Record of the Way and Fate" (5 juan), "Record of Pacification on the Western Frontier" (90 juan), "Correction of the Record of the Southern Migration" (1 juan), and one hundred juan of poems and prose.

sentences.zh: 葉味道，初諱賀孫，以字行，更字知道，溫州人。

translations.literal: Ye Weidao, whose original taboo name was Hesun, went by his style name and later changed his courtesy name to Zhidao, was a native of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Weidao, originally named Hesun, was known by his style name and later adopted the courtesy name Zhidao; he came from Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 少刻誌好古學，師事朱熹。

translations.literal: From youth he was dedicated to antiquarian learning and took Zhu Xi as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he devoted himself to classical learning and studied under Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 試禮部第一。

translations.literal: In the Ministry of Rites examination he placed first.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked first in the Ministry of Rites examination.

sentences.zh: 時偽學禁行，味道對學製策，率本程頤無所避。

translations.literal: At that time the ban on heterodox learning was in force; Weidao in the academic policy examination essay consistently based himself on Cheng Yi without avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: When the ban on heterodox learning was in force, Weidao's policy examination essay consistently drew on Cheng Yi without holding back.

sentences.zh: 知舉胡紘見而黜之，曰：“此必偽徒也。

translations.literal: Chief examiner Hu Hong saw it and rejected him, saying, "This must be a heterodox follower.
translations.idiomatic: Chief examiner Hu Hong saw it and failed him, saying, "This must be a follower of the banned school.

sentences.zh: ”既下第，復從熹於武夷山中。

translations.literal: " After failing the examination, he again followed Xi in the Wuyi mountains.
translations.idiomatic: " After failing the examination, he again studied with Zhu Xi in the Wuyi mountains.

sentences.zh: 學禁開，登嘉定十三年進士第，調鄂州教授。

translations.literal: When the learning ban was lifted, he passed the jinshi examination in the thirteenth year of Jiading and was appointed professor at Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the learning ban was lifted, he passed the jinshi examination in 1220 and was posted as professor at Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 理宗訪問熹之徒及所著書，部使者遂以味道行誼聞，差主管三省架閣文字。

translations.literal: Emperor Lizong inquired about Xi's disciples and their written works; the circuit commissioner then reported Weidao's conduct and righteousness, and he was appointed to oversee the Three Departments archive documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Lizong inquired about Zhu Xi's disciples and their writings, the circuit commissioner reported Weidao's character and integrity, and he was appointed to oversee archival documents for the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 遷宗學諭，輪對，言：“人主之務學，天下之福也。

translations.literal: Transferred to tutor of the Imperial Clan school, in a rotating audience he said, "A ruler's task of learning is the world's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to tutor at the Imperial Clan school, in a rotating audience he said, "When a ruler devotes himself to learning, it is a blessing for the realm.

sentences.zh: 必堅誌氣以守所學，謹幾微以驗所學，正綱常以勵所學，用忠言以充所學。

translations.literal: One must firm resolve and spirit to guard what is learned, watch subtle signs to test what is learned, rectify the cardinal norms to encourage what is learned, and use loyal words to enrich what is learned.
translations.idiomatic: He must hold fast to his resolve to preserve what he has learned, watch the subtlest signs to test it, uphold the cardinal norms to strengthen it, and welcome loyal counsel to complete it.

sentences.zh: ”至若口奏，則又述帝王傳心之要，與四代作歌作銘之旨，其終有曰：“言宣則力減，文勝則意虛。

translations.literal: " As for oral presentation, he also expounded the essence of emperors transmitting the mind and the purpose of the four dynasties composing songs and inscriptions; at the end he said, "When words are spread out, force is diminished; when rhetoric overwhelms, meaning becomes hollow.
translations.idiomatic: " In his oral presentation he also explained how emperors transmit the mind and why the four ancient dynasties composed songs and inscriptions; he concluded, "When speech is overextended, its force is spent; when rhetoric overwhelms, meaning grows empty.

sentences.zh: ”從臣有薦味道可為講官，乃授太學博士，兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: " Attendant ministers recommended that Weidao could serve as lecturer; he was then made Doctor of the Imperial University and concurrent lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: " Attendant ministers recommended Weidao as a lecturer, and he was appointed Doctor of the Imperial University and concurrent lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 故事，說書之職止於《通鑒》，而不及經。

translations.literal: By precedent, the lecturer's duty stopped at the "Comprehensive Mirror" and did not extend to the classics.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, lecturers were limited to the "Comprehensive Mirror" and did not cover the classics.

sentences.zh: 味道請先說《論語》，詔從之。

translations.literal: Weidao requested to lecture first on the "Analects"; an edict followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: Weidao asked to lecture first on the "Analects," and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝忽問鬼神之理，疑伯有之事涉於誕。

translations.literal: The emperor suddenly asked about the principle of ghosts and spirits, doubting that the affair of Bo You verged on the fantastic.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suddenly asked about ghosts and spirits, suspecting that the story of Bo You was rather far-fetched.

sentences.zh: 味道對曰：“陰陽二氣之散聚，雖天地不能易。

translations.literal: Weidao replied, "The dispersion and gathering of the two qi, yin and yang—even Heaven and Earth cannot alter them.
translations.idiomatic: Weidao replied, "The dispersal and gathering of yin and yang—even Heaven and Earth cannot change them.

sentences.zh: 有死而猶不散者，其常也。

translations.literal: That some die yet their qi still does not disperse is the constant pattern.
translations.idiomatic: That the dead sometimes do not fully disperse is the normal case.

sentences.zh: 有不得其死而鬱結不散者，其變也。

translations.literal: That some do not meet their proper death and their pent-up qi does not disperse is the variant pattern.
translations.idiomatic: That those who die unjustly may remain pent up and undispersed is the exceptional case.

sentences.zh: 故聖人設為宗祧，以別親疏遠邇，正所以教民親愛，參讚化育。

translations.literal: Therefore the sages established ancestral temples to distinguish near and distant kin, precisely to teach the people affection and to assist in nurturing transformation.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the sages established ancestral temples to distinguish kin near and far—precisely to teach the people mutual affection and to help nurture life.

sentences.zh: 今伯有得罪而死，其氣不散，為妖為厲，使國人上下為之不寧，於是為之立子泄以奉其後，則庶乎鬼有所知，而神莫不寧矣。

translations.literal: Now Bo You died in guilt, his qi did not disperse, becoming an apparition and a curse, making the people above and below the state restless for him; therefore a successor Zixie was established to maintain his line—then perhaps ghosts would have awareness and spirits would all be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Bo You died under a charge, his spirit did not disperse, and he became a haunting curse that unsettled the whole state; so they established Zixie as his heir to carry on his line—then ghosts might take heed and all spirits find rest.

sentences.zh: ”蓋諷皇子竑事也。

translations.literal: " This was an indirect criticism of the affair of Prince Hao.
translations.idiomatic: " This was an indirect criticism of the affair of Crown Prince Hao.

sentences.zh: 三京用師，廷臣邊閫交進機會之說。

translations.literal: When troops were deployed for the Three Capitals campaign, court ministers and frontier commanders vied to advance opportunistic proposals.
translations.idiomatic: When the court mobilized for the Three Capitals campaign, ministers and frontier commanders competed to urge seizing the moment.

sentences.zh: 味道進議狀，以為：“開邊浸闊，應援倍難，科配日繁，饋餉日迫，民一不堪命，龐勳、黃巢之禍立見，是先搖其本，無益於外也。

translations.literal: Weidao submitted a memorial of opinion, stating, "Opening the frontier expands daily, reinforcement becomes doubly difficult, levies grow more numerous by the day, supplies grow more urgent by the day—once the people cannot bear their lot, the disasters of Pang Xun and Huang Chao will appear at once. This first shakes the root and benefits nothing abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Weidao submitted a memorial arguing that "as the frontier war widens, reinforcements grow ever harder to supply, levies multiply daily, and logistics grow ever tighter; once the people can bear no more, disasters like those of Pang Xun and Huang Chao will follow at once. This shakes the foundation first and gains nothing abroad.

sentences.zh: ”經筵奏事，無日不申言之，而洛師尋以敗聞。

translations.literal: " At the Classics Mat he memorialized daily without exception, and soon news came of the Luoyang army's defeat.
translations.idiomatic: " At the Classics Mat he pressed the point every day without fail, and soon came word that the Luoyang force had been defeated.

sentences.zh: 於是人謂味道見微慮遠。

translations.literal: Then people said Weidao saw the subtle and thought far ahead.
translations.idiomatic: People then said that Weidao had seen the warning signs and thought far ahead.

sentences.zh: 味道所奏陳，無一言不開導引翼，求切於君身；

translations.literal: In everything Weidao memorialized, not one word failed to guide and nurture, all seeking what was urgently needed for the ruler's person;
translations.idiomatic: In every memorial Weidao submitted, each word sought to guide and support the ruler himself;

sentences.zh: 旁引折旋，推致於治道。

translations.literal: Drawing parallels and circling back, he extended to the Way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: By drawing parallels and circling back, he always led the discussion to the principles of good government.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書著作佐郎而卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant in the Secretariat Composition Office and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Assistant in the Secretariat Composition Office and then died.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，帝震悼，出內帑銀帛賻其喪，升一官以任其後，故事所未有也。

translations.literal: When the death notice arrived, the emperor was shaken with grief, dispensed silver and silk from the inner treasury to subsidize the funeral, and promoted one rank to support his descendants—precedent had never known this.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death arrived, the emperor was deeply grieved, sent silver and silk from the inner treasury to help with the funeral, and promoted his heir one rank—something without precedent.

sentences.zh: 所著《四書說》、《大學講義》、《祭法宗廟廟享郊社外傳》、《經筵口奏》、《故事講義》。

translations.literal: Works he authored included "Commentary on the Four Books," "Lectures on the Great Learning," "External Commentary on the Rites of Sacrifice, Ancestral Temples, Temple Offerings, and Suburban and Altar Rites," "Oral Memorials at the Classics Mat," and "Lectures on Precedents."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the "Commentary on the Four Books," "Lectures on the Great Learning," "External Commentary on the Rites of Sacrifice, Ancestral Temples, Temple Offerings, and Suburban and Altar Rites," "Oral Memorials at the Classics Mat," and "Lectures on Precedents."

sentences.zh: 王應麟，字伯厚，慶元府人。

translations.literal: Wang Yinglin, styled Bohou, was a native of Qingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yinglin, courtesy name Bohou, came from Qingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 九歲通《六經》，淳祐元年舉進士，從王野受學。

translations.literal: At nine he mastered the Six Classics; in the first year of Chunyou he passed the jinshi examination and studied under Wang Ye.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he had mastered the Six Classics; in 1241 he passed the jinshi examination and studied under Wang Ye.

sentences.zh: 調西安主簿，民以年少易視之，輸賦後時。

translations.literal: Appointed chief clerk of Xi'an County, the people thought him young and looked lightly on him, and tax payments were late.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as chief clerk of Xi'an County, the people looked down on him for his youth, and tax payments fell behind.

sentences.zh: 應麟白郡守，繩以法，遂立辦。

translations.literal: Yinglin reported to the prefect, bound them by law, and it was promptly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglin reported the matter to the prefect, enforced the law, and the payments were promptly collected.

sentences.zh: 諸校欲為亂，知縣事翁甫倉皇計不知所出，應麟以禮諭服之。

translations.literal: Various guard units wanted to rebel; Weng Fu, who handled county affairs, was panicked and knew no plan; Yinglin with ritual persuasion made them submit.
translations.idiomatic: When several guard units plotted mutiny, Weng Fu, acting magistrate, was at a loss; Yinglin persuaded them with reason and propriety until they submitted.

sentences.zh: 差監平江百萬東倉。

translations.literal: He was appointed to supervise the Pingjiang Million-East Granary.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to supervise the Million-East Granary at Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 調浙西提舉常平茶鹽主管帳司，部使者鄭霖異待之。

translations.literal: Transferred to account supervisor under the Zhexi Grain Commissioner for Ever-Normal Granaries, Tea, and Salt, circuit commissioner Zheng Lin treated him exceptionally.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as account supervisor under the Zhexi Commissioner for Ever-Normal Granaries, Tea, and Salt, and circuit commissioner Zheng Lin treated him with special regard.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，調揚州教授。

translations.literal: He mourned his father; when the mourning period ended, he was appointed professor at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father and completing the mourning period, he was posted as professor at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，應麟登第，言曰：“今之事舉子業者，沽名譽，得則一切委棄，制度典故漫不省，非國家所望於通儒。

translations.literal: When Yinglin first passed the examination, he said, "Those who pursue the examination trade today trade on reputation; once they succeed they abandon everything, neither understanding institutions nor precedents—this is not what the state expects of broadly learned Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: When Yinglin first passed the examinations, he said, "Those who pursue the examination career today chase reputation; once they succeed they cast everything aside and know nothing of institutions or precedent—this is not what the state expects of true scholars.

sentences.zh: ”於是閉門發憤，誓以博學宏辭科自見，假館閣書讀之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he shut his door in determined study, vowing to prove himself through the Broad Learning and Eloquent Diction examination, borrowing imperial library books to read.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he shut his door and studied with fierce resolve, vowing to distinguish himself in the Broad Learning and Eloquent Diction examination and borrowing imperial library books to read.

sentences.zh: 寶祐四年中是科。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoyou he passed that examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1256 he passed that examination.

sentences.zh: 應麟與弟應鳳同日生，開慶元年亦中是科，詔褒諭之，添差浙西安撫司幹辦公事。

translations.literal: Yinglin and his younger brother Yingfeng were born on the same day; in the first year of Kaiqing Yingfeng also passed that examination; an edict praised them, and he was specially assigned as staff officer on the Zhexi Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglin and his younger brother Yingfeng shared the same birthday; in 1259 Yingfeng also passed that examination, the court issued an edict of praise, and Yinglin was specially assigned as staff officer on the Zhexi Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 帝御集英殿策士，召應麟覆考。

translations.literal: The emperor held the palace examination at the Hall of Assembled Excellence and summoned Yinglin to re-examine the papers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held the palace examination in the Hall of Assembled Excellence and summoned Yinglin to review the papers again.

sentences.zh: 考第既上，帝欲易第七卷置其首。

translations.literal: When the rankings were submitted, the emperor wanted to swap the seventh scroll to first place.
translations.idiomatic: When the rankings were submitted, the emperor wanted to move the seventh scroll to first place.

sentences.zh: 應麟讀之，乃頓首曰：“是卷古誼若龜鏡，忠肝如鐵石，臣敢為得士賀。

translations.literal: Yinglin read it and kowtowed, saying, "This scroll's ancient righteousness is like a tortoise mirror, its loyal heart like iron and stone—I venture to congratulate Your Majesty on gaining such a man.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglin read it and kowtowed, saying, "This scroll's ancient righteousness is clear as a mirror, its loyal heart firm as iron and stone—I venture to congratulate Your Majesty on finding such a man.

sentences.zh: ”遂以第七卷為首選。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the seventh scroll was made first rank.
translations.idiomatic: " The seventh scroll was accordingly ranked first.

sentences.zh: 及唱名，乃文天祥也。

translations.literal: When the names were announced, it was Wen Tianxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the names were read aloud, the candidate was Wen Tianxiang.

sentences.zh: 遷主管三省、樞密院架閣文字。

translations.literal: He was transferred to oversee the Three Departments and Privy Council archive documents.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to oversee archival documents for the Three Departments and the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 遷國子錄，進武學博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to registrar of the National University and promoted to Doctor of the Military Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to registrar of the National University and then to Doctor of the Military Academy.

sentences.zh: 疏言：“陛下閱理多，願治久。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said, "Your Majesty has reviewed governance much and long desired good rule.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he said, "Your Majesty has long studied governance and long desired good rule.

sentences.zh: 當事勢之艱，輿圖蹙於外患，人才乏而民力殫，宜強為善，增修德，無自沮怠；

translations.literal: Facing hard circumstances, the realm shrinking under external troubles, talent scarce and popular strength exhausted—you should force yourself to do good, increase and cultivate virtue, and not slacken in despair;
translations.idiomatic: In hard times, with the realm pressed by foreign threats, talent scarce and the people's strength spent, you should force yourself to do good, cultivate virtue all the more, and not fall into despair;

sentences.zh: 恢弘士氣，下情畢達，操綱紀而明委任，謹左右而防壅蔽，求哲人以輔後嗣。

translations.literal: Expand scholar-official morale, let lower sentiments all reach you, grasp standards and clarify appointments, watch those close and guard against blockage, and seek wise men to assist the successor.
translations.idiomatic: lift the spirit of the scholar-officials, let every grievance from below reach you, hold fast to standards and make appointments clear, watch those close at hand and guard against obstruction, and seek wise men to assist the heir.

sentences.zh: ”既對，帝問其父名，曰：“爾父以陳善為忠，可謂繼美。

translations.literal: " After the audience, the emperor asked his father's name and said, "Your father took presenting what is good as loyalty—this may be called inheriting excellence.
translations.idiomatic: " After the audience, the emperor asked his father's name and said, "Your father made presenting what is good his standard of loyalty—truly you inherit a fine legacy.
(The emperor's words ended.)

sentences.zh: 丁大全欲致應麟，不可得。

translations.literal: Ding Daquan wanted to win Yinglin over but could not.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Daquan tried to recruit Yinglin but failed.

sentences.zh: 遷太常寺主簿，麵對，言：“淮戍方警，蜀道孔艱，海表上流皆有藩籬唇齒之憂。

translations.literal: Promoted to Registrar of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, facing the emperor in audience he said, "The Huai garrison is just now on alert, the Shu route is extremely difficult, and the upper reaches of the maritime frontier all have concerns like outer ramparts and inner lips."
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Registrar of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, in audience before the emperor he said, "The Huai defenses are on alert, the road into Shu is perilously hard, and the upper reaches of the maritime frontier all face the mutual-defense anxieties of rampart and lip."

sentences.zh: 軍功未集而吝賞，民力既困而重斂，非修攘計也。

translations.literal: Military merit not yet gathered yet rewards are stinted; popular strength already exhausted yet levies are increased—this is no plan for cultivation and repelling.
translations.idiomatic: To stint on rewards before military achievements are secured, and to levy heavier taxes when the people's strength is already spent, is no strategy for strengthening the state and repelling the enemy.

sentences.zh: 陛下勿以宴安自逸，勿以容悅之言自寬。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, do not take ease in peaceful comfort, and do not take pleasing words as consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must not grow complacent in ease and comfort, nor take flattering words as reassurance.

sentences.zh: ”帝愀然曰：“邊事甚可憂。

translations.literal: " The emperor said solemnly, "Border affairs are very worrisome.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said gravely, "The border situation is deeply troubling.

sentences.zh: ”應麟言：“無事深憂，臨事不懼。

translations.literal: " Yinglin said, "In calm times worry deeply; when crisis comes do not fear.
translations.idiomatic: " Yinglin said, "In peace worry deeply; when crisis comes do not panic.

sentences.zh: 願汲汲預防，毋為壅蔽所欺。

translations.literal: I pray you act urgently in prevention and do not be deceived by blockage.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty will act urgently to prepare and not be misled by those who block the truth.

sentences.zh: ”時大全諱言邊事，於是應麟罷。

translations.literal: " At that time Daquan forbade talk of border affairs, and so Yinglin was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Daquan suppressed discussion of border affairs, and Yinglin was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大全敗，起應麟通判台州。

translations.literal: Before long Daquan fell, and Yinglin was recalled as vice prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Daquan fell from power, and Yinglin was recalled as vice prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 召為太常博士，擢秘書郎，俄兼沂靖惠王府教授。

translations.literal: Summoned as Doctor of Imperial Sacrifices, promoted to Secretariat Gentleman, and soon also tutor of the Prince of Yijinghui's household.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Doctor of Imperial Sacrifices, promoted to Secretariat Gentleman, and soon also appointed tutor in the household of the Prince of Yijinghui.

sentences.zh: 彗星見，應詔極論執政、侍從、台諫之罪，積私財、行公田之害。

translations.literal: When a comet appeared, by edict he vigorously discussed the guilt of the chief administrators, attendants, and remonstrance officials, and the harm of amassing private wealth and implementing public fields.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appeared, he responded to an edict with a forceful indictment of the chief ministers, attendants, and remonstrance officials, and of the harm done by hoarding private wealth and imposing public fields.

sentences.zh: 又言：“應天變莫先回人心，回人心莫先直受言。

translations.literal: He also said, "In responding to Heaven's changes, nothing comes before turning back the people's hearts; in turning back hearts, nothing comes before openly receiving remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "To respond to Heaven's warning, nothing comes before winning back the people's hearts; to win back hearts, nothing comes before receiving remonstrance openly.

sentences.zh: 箝天下之口，沮直臣之氣，如應天何？

translations.literal: Clamping the world's mouths and discouraging upright ministers' spirit—how can one respond to Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: If you silence the realm and break the spirit of upright ministers, how can you respond to Heaven?

sentences.zh: ”時直言者多迕權臣意，故應麟及之。

translations.literal: " At that time many who spoke frankly offended powerful ministers, and so Yinglin was implicated.
translations.idiomatic: " Many who spoke frankly then ran afoul of powerful ministers, and Yinglin was caught up in the backlash.

sentences.zh: 遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant in the Composition Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Assistant in the Composition Office.

sentences.zh: 度宗即位，攝禮部郎官，草百官表。

translations.literal: When Duzong ascended the throne, he served as acting Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites and drafted the hundred officials' memorials.
translations.idiomatic: When Duzong ascended the throne, Yinglin served as acting Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites and drafted the memorials of the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 舊制，請聽政，四表已上。

translations.literal: By old regulation, in requesting to attend to governance, four memorials or more were required.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations, a request to assume governance required four memorials or more.

sentences.zh: 一夕入臨，宰臣諭旨增撰三表，應麟操筆立就。

translations.literal: One evening he entered mourning audience; the chief minister conveyed an order to add three memorials, and Yinglin took brush and completed them at once.
translations.idiomatic: One evening, entering the mourning audience, the chief minister ordered three additional memorials drafted, and Yinglin wrote them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 丞相總護還，辭位表三道，使者立以俟，應麟從容授之。

translations.literal: When the chief councilor returned from overall command, there were three resignation memorials; the messenger stood waiting, and Yinglin calmly handed them over.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief councilor returned from overall command, three resignation memorials were needed; the messenger stood waiting, and Yinglin calmly handed them over.

sentences.zh: 丞相驚服，即授兼禮部郎官、兼直學士院。

translations.literal: The chief councilor was astonished and impressed, and immediately appointed him concurrent Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilor was deeply impressed and at once made him concurrent Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 馬廷鸞知貢舉，詔應麟兼權直，俄兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: Ma Tingluan was chief examiner; an edict made Yinglin acting Hanlin duty officer, and soon also lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Tingluan served as chief examiner, an edict appointed Yinglin acting Hanlin duty officer, and soon also lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 遷著作郎，守軍器少監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Composition Gentleman and acting Vice Director of Armaments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Composition Gentleman and acting Vice Director of Armaments.

sentences.zh: 經筵值人日雪，帝問有何故事，應麟以唐李嶠、李乂等應製詩對。

translations.literal: At the Classics Mat on Human Day when it snowed, the emperor asked what precedents there were; Yinglin answered with the Tang court poems composed on command by Li Jiao, Li Yi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: At the Classics Mat on Human Day, when snow fell, the emperor asked what precedents existed; Yinglin answered with the Tang court poems composed on command by Li Jiao, Li Yi, and others.

sentences.zh: 因奏：“春雪過多，民生饑寒，方寸仁愛，宜謹感召。

translations.literal: He then memorialized, "Spring snow is excessive; the people's lives suffer cold and hunger—your inch-square heart of benevolence should carefully seek responsive influence.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "With so much spring snow, the people suffer cold and hunger; Your Majesty's compassionate heart should earnestly seek to move Heaven.

sentences.zh: ”遷將作監。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then promoted to Director of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 帝視朝，謂應麟曰：“為學要灼見古人之心。

translations.literal: At court audience the emperor said to Yinglin, "In learning one must clearly see the minds of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: At court the emperor said to Yinglin, "In study one must truly grasp the minds of the ancients.

sentences.zh: ”應麟對曰“嚴恭寅畏，不敢怠皇，克勤克儉，無自縱逸，強以馭下，製事以斷，此古人之心。

translations.literal: " Yinglin replied, "Strict reverence and cautious awe, daring not to slacken toward the sovereign, being industrious and frugal, not indulging oneself in dissipation, governing subordinates with firmness, deciding affairs with decisiveness — this is the mind of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: " Yinglin answered, "Solemn respect and dutiful caution, never neglecting the ruler, practicing diligence and thrift, refusing self-indulgence, ruling firmly over subordinates, and cutting through affairs with decision — that is the ancients' ideal.

sentences.zh: 然操舍易忽於眇綿，兢業每忘於遊衍。

translations.literal: Yet holding and releasing are easily neglected amid subtle details; diligent devotion is often forgotten amid wandering amusements.
translations.idiomatic: But resolve is easily lost in minute distractions, and earnest diligence is often set aside for idle pastimes.

sentences.zh: ”帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor commendably accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and adopted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 既而轉對，言：“人君防未萌之欲，存不已之誠。

translations.literal: Soon, in a rotating audience, he said: "A ruler should guard against desires before they sprout and preserve unceasing sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, in a rotating memorial audience, he said, "The sovereign must check incipient desires and sustain ceaseless sincerity.

sentences.zh: ”擢兼侍立修注官，升權直學士院，遷秘書少監兼侍講。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to also serve as attendant editor-assistant, elevated to acting chief of the Hanlin Academy, and transferred to vice director of the Secretariat while also serving as lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed concurrent attendant editor, promoted to acting chief of the Hanlin Academy, and transferred to vice director of the Secretariat with a concurrent lecturing post.

sentences.zh: 上疏論市舶，不報。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial on maritime trade; no response.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on maritime trade offices; the court did not reply.

sentences.zh: 會賈似道拜平章事，葉夢鼎、江萬里各求去，似道亦求去。

translations.literal: When Jia Sidao was appointed Grand Councillor, Ye Mengding and Jiang Wanli each sought to leave office, and Sidao also sought to leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Sidao received appointment as Grand Councillor, Ye Mengding and Jiang Wanli each asked to resign, and Sidao himself also sought to step down.

sentences.zh: 應麟奏，孝宗朝闕相者亦逾年，帝亟取以諭之。

translations.literal: Yinglin memorialized that during Emperor Xiaozong's reign the vacancy of chief councillor had also lasted over a year; the emperor immediately fetched the record to show him.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglin cited the precedent that under Emperor Xiaozong the chief councillorship had likewise stood vacant for more than a year; the emperor at once had the record brought out to instruct him.

sentences.zh: 似道聞應麟言，大惡之，語包恢曰：“我去朝士若王伯厚者多矣，但此人素著文學名，不欲使天下謂我棄士。

translations.literal: Sidao heard Yinglin's words and greatly hated him; he said to Bao Hui: "When I leave, court officials like Wang Bohou will be many, but this man has long had a literary reputation — I do not wish the realm to say I have abandoned scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao, hearing Yinglin's remark, loathed him deeply and told Bao Hui, "When I go, courtiers like Wang Bohou will be legion, but this man has long been known for letters — I do not want the world to say I cast scholars aside.

sentences.zh: 彼盍思少自貶！

translations.literal: Why does he not think of lowering himself a little!
translations.idiomatic: Let him consider humbling himself a little!

sentences.zh: ”恢以告，應麟笑曰：“迕相之患小，負君之罪大。

translations.literal: " Hui told him; Yinglin laughed and said: "The harm of opposing the chief councillor is small; the crime of betraying the sovereign is great.
translations.idiomatic: " When Hui relayed this, Yinglin laughed and said, "The trouble of crossing the chief councillor is slight; the guilt of failing the sovereign is grave.

sentences.zh: ”遷起居舍人，兼權中書舍人。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to diarist and also acting drafting secretary.
translations.idiomatic: " He was moved to diarist of attendance and concurrent acting drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 冬雷，應麟言：“十月之雷，惟東漢數見。

translations.literal: Winter thunder — Yinglin said: "Thunder in the tenth month has been seen many times only in the Eastern Han.
translations.idiomatic: When thunder sounded in winter, Yinglin said, "Tenth-month thunder was seen repeatedly only in the Eastern Han.

sentences.zh: 命令不專，奸衺並進，卑逾尊，外陵內之象。

translations.literal: When commands are not concentrated, wickedness advances together — the image of the low surpassing the high, the outer overwhelming the inner.
translations.idiomatic: When authority is divided, treachery rises together — a sign of the base overtaking the exalted, the outer pressing upon the inner.

sentences.zh: 當清天君，謹天命，體天德，以回天心。

translations.literal: One should purify the sovereign of Heaven, reverence Heaven's command, embody Heaven's virtue, to turn back Heaven's heart.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler must cleanse himself before Heaven, honor Heaven's mandate, embody Heaven's virtue, and so win Heaven's favor back.

sentences.zh: 守成必法祖宗，禦治必總威福。

translations.literal: Preserving the achievement must follow the ancestors; governing must concentrate authority and favor.
translations.idiomatic: To keep what has been won, one must take the ancestors as model; to rule well, one must gather power and favor in the throne.

sentences.zh: ”似道聞之，斥逐之意決矣。

translations.literal: " Sidao heard this and his determination to oust him was settled.
translations.idiomatic: " Sidao heard it and resolved at once to drive him out.

sentences.zh: 應麟牒閣門直前奏對，謂用人莫先察君子小人。

translations.literal: Yinglin submitted a memorial at the Gate Department to petition for direct audience, saying that in employing men one must first discern gentlemen from petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglin sent a memorial through the Gate Department requesting direct audience, arguing that in appointments one must first distinguish the upright from the base.

sentences.zh: 方袖疏待班，台臣亟疏駁之，由是二史直前之製遂廢。

translations.literal: Just as he tucked his memorial in his sleeve and waited in court ranks, censorial officials hurriedly submitted memorials to rebut him — by this the system of diarists petitioning directly was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: As he held his memorial and awaited his turn in court, censorial officials rushed forward with counter-memorials, and the custom of diarists petitioning directly was abolished.

sentences.zh: 以秘閣修撰主管崇禧觀。

translations.literal: He was made compiler of the Privy Archive, concurrently administrator of the Chongxi Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed compiler in the Privy Archive and put in charge of the Chongxi Abbey.

sentences.zh: 久之，起知徽州。

translations.literal: After a long while he was recalled and appointed prefect of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was recalled to serve as prefect of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 其父撝嚐守是郡，父老皆曰：“此清白太守子也。

translations.literal: His father Hui had once been prefect of that commandery; the elders all said: "This is the son of the incorruptible prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui had governed that prefecture; the local elders said, "Here is the son of the incorrupt prefect.

sentences.zh: ”摧豪右，省租賦，民大悅。

translations.literal: " He crushed powerful elites, reduced rent and taxes, and the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " He broke the power of local magnates, cut rents and levies, and the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 召為秘書監，權中書舍人，力辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was summoned as director of the Secretariat and acting drafting secretary; he strenuously declined but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as director of the Secretariat and acting drafting secretary, he pleaded hard to decline but was refused.

sentences.zh: 兼國史編修、實錄檢討兼侍講。

translations.literal: Concurrently compiler of the national history, examiner of the veritable records, and lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as compiler of the national history, examiner of the veritable records, and court lecturer.

sentences.zh: 遷起居郎兼權吏部侍郎，指陳成敗逆順之說，且曰：“國家所恃者大江，襄、樊其喉舌，議不容緩。

translations.literal: Transferred to court gentleman and acting vice minister of personnel; he pointed out theories of success and failure, reversal and compliance, and said: "What the state relies on is the Great River; Xiangyang and Fancheng are its throat and tongue — discussion cannot brook delay.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to court gentleman and acting vice minister of personnel, he laid out arguments of triumph and disaster, advance and retreat, and said, "The empire rests on the Yangtze; Xiangyang and Fancheng are its gateway — deliberation cannot wait.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方從容如常時，事幾一失，豈能自安？

translations.literal: The court was still proceeding at ease as in normal times; once the crisis of the moment was lost, how could one rest secure?
translations.idiomatic: The court still moved as leisurely as in ordinary days; let the moment slip once, and who could feel secure?

sentences.zh: ”朝臣無以邊事言者，帝不懌。

translations.literal: " No court officials spoke of frontier affairs; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " No minister would speak of the border crisis, and the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 似道復謀斥逐，適應麟以母憂去。

translations.literal: Sidao again plotted to expel him; just then Yinglin departed on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao again schemed to remove him, but Yinglin left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 及似道潰師江上，授中書舍人兼直學士院，即引疏陳十事，急征討、明政刑、厲廉恥、通下情、求將材、練軍實、備糧餉、舉實材、擇牧守、防海道，其目也。

translations.literal: When Sidao's army was routed on the river, Yinglin was appointed drafting secretary and concurrently chief of the Hanlin Academy; he immediately submitted a memorial setting forth ten matters — urgent mobilization for punitive campaigns, clarifying government and punishments, sharpening integrity and shame, opening channels to popular sentiment, seeking general talent, training military reality, preparing grain and provisions, promoting genuine talent, selecting prefects and magistrates, and guarding sea routes — these were the items.
translations.idiomatic: After Sidao's forces collapsed on the Yangtze, Yinglin was made drafting secretary and chief of the Hanlin Academy; he at once submitted ten urgent proposals: rally troops, clarify law and punishment, restore integrity, hear the people, find generals, drill the army, stock provisions, employ real talent, choose good governors, and secure the coast.

sentences.zh: 且言：“圖大患者必略細故，求實效者必去虛文。

translations.literal: He also said: "Those who plan for great calamities must set aside minor matters; those who seek real effects must remove empty documents.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "To confront great peril one must overlook small grievances; to achieve real results one must strip away hollow paperwork.

sentences.zh: ”因請集諸路勤王之師，有能率先而至者，宜厚賞以作勇敢之氣，並力進戰，惟能戰，斯可守。

translations.literal: " He therefore requested assembling troops from all routes rallying to the throne; those able to arrive first should be generously rewarded to stir courage, and all should advance together in battle — only by being able to fight can one defend.
translations.idiomatic: " He asked that loyal armies from every circuit be gathered; those who came first should be richly rewarded to rouse valor, and all should fight together — only if one can fight can one hold.

sentences.zh: 進兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰兼侍讀，遷禮部侍郎兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: Promoted to concurrently compiler of the national history and co-compiler of the Veritable Records Academy while also serving as reader-in-waiting; transferred to vice minister of rites while also drafting secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to concurrent compiler of the national history and co-compiler in the Veritable Records Academy with a reader-in-waiting post, then became vice minister of rites and drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 日食，應麟詔論答天戒五事，陳備禦十策，皆不及用。

translations.literal: At a solar eclipse Yinglin, in an edict response on Heaven's warning, set forth five matters and ten strategies of defense — none were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: During an eclipse Yinglin answered the imperial edict on Heaven's rebuke with five points and ten defense measures, but none were used.

sentences.zh: 尋轉尚書兼給事中。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to minister of works while also serving as receiver of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to minister of works with a concurrent post as receiver of memorials.

sentences.zh: 左丞相留夢炎用徐囊為御史，擢江西製置使黃萬石等，應麟繳奏曰：“囊與夢炎同鄉，有私人之嫌，萬石粗戾無學，南昌失守，誤國罪大。

translations.literal: Left chief councillor Liu Mengyan employed Xu Nang as censor and promoted Huang Wanshi of Jiangxi as commissioner-in-chief, among others; Yinglin returned the memorial saying: "Nang is from the same native district as Mengyan — there is suspicion of personal favor; Wanshi is coarse, violent, and unlearned; losing Nanchang was a great crime against the state.
translations.idiomatic: Left chief councillor Liu Mengyan appointed Xu Nang censor and promoted Jiangxi commissioner Huang Wanshi and others; Yinglin returned the order, saying, "Nang shares Mengyan's home district — a private tie is suspected; Wanshi is rough, brutal, and ignorant, and the loss of Nanchang was a grave betrayal of the realm.

sentences.zh: 今方欲引以自助，善類為所搏噬者，必攜持而去。

translations.literal: Now you wish to bring them in to help yourselves; good men whom they attack and devour will surely depart carrying their grievances.
translations.idiomatic: If you now recruit them to bolster yourselves, upright men they harry and ruin will leave in bitterness.

sentences.zh: 吳浚貪墨輕躁，豈宜用之？

translations.literal: Wu Jun is greedy, corrupt, frivolous, and rash — how can he be employed?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jun is venal, reckless, and impulsive — how can he be put in office?

sentences.zh: 況夢炎舛令慢諫，讜言弗敢告，今之賣降者，多其任用之士。

translations.literal: Moreover Mengyan issues mistaken orders and treats remonstrance lightly; straight speech he dare not report; many of those who now sell surrender were men he employed.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Mengyan gives bad orders and scorns remonstrance; honest counsel he will not relay, and many who now offer surrender are men he raised.

sentences.zh: ”疏再上，不報。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted again; no response.
translations.idiomatic: " He resubmitted the memorial; again there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 出關俟命，再奏曰：“因危急而紊紀綱，以偏見而咈公議，臣封駁不行，與大臣異論，勢不當留。

translations.literal: Leaving the pass to await orders, he submitted again: "Because of crisis disordering standards, because of partial views rejecting public opinion — my memorial returns are not executed, and I differ from great ministers; the situation is that I should not remain.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the capital gate awaiting orders, he wrote again, "In peril the norms are thrown into confusion; with partial views public debate is silenced — my returns are ignored and I stand apart from the chief ministers; I cannot stay.

sentences.zh: ”疏入，又不報，遂東歸。

translations.literal: " The memorial entered; again no response; he then returned east.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial went in and again went unanswered; he then went home to the east.

sentences.zh: 詔中使譚純德以翰林學士召，識者以為奪其要路，寵以清秩，非所以待賢者。

translations.literal: An edict sent eunuch Tan Chunde to summon him as Hanlin academician; perceptive men thought this seized his critical path and favored him with a pure rank — not how to treat the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The throne dispatched eunuch Tan Chunde to summon him as Hanlin academician; observers said this pulled him from the vital post and rewarded him with an honorary rank — no way to honor a worthy man.

sentences.zh: 應麟亦力辭，後二十年卒。

translations.literal: Yinglin also strenuously declined; twenty years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglin again refused firmly; he died twenty years later.

sentences.zh: 所著有《深寧集》一百卷、《王堂類稿》二十三卷、《掖垣類稿》二十二卷、《詩考》五卷、《詩地理考》五卷、《漢藝文藝誌考證》十卷、《通鑒地理考》一百卷、《通鑒地理通釋》十六卷、《通鑒答問》四卷、《困學紀聞》二十卷、《蒙訓》七十卷、《集解踐阼篇》、《補注急就篇》六卷、《補注王會篇》、《小學紺珠》十卷、《玉海》二百卷、《詞學指南》四卷、《詞學題苑》四十卷、《姓氏急就篇》六卷、《漢製考》四卷、《六經天文編》六卷、《小學諷詠》四卷。

translations.literal: His writings included "Collected Works of Shenning" in one hundred juan, "Drafts from the Royal Hall" in twenty-three juan, "Drafts from the Palace Secretariat" in twenty-two juan, "Investigation of the Odes" in five juan, "Geographical Investigation of the Odes" in five juan, "Textual Verification of the "Bibliographic Treatise on Literature" in the "History of Han"" in ten juan, "Geographical Investigation of the "Comprehensive Mirror"" in one hundred juan, "General Explanation of Geography in the "Comprehensive Mirror"" in sixteen juan, "Questions and Answers on the "Comprehensive Mirror"" in four juan, "Observations from Difficult Study" in twenty juan, "Elementary Instruction" in seventy juan, "Collected Exegesis: The Accession Chapter," "Supplement and Commentary to the "Quick Mastery Primer"" in six juan, "Supplement and Commentary to the "Royal Assembly Chapter,"" "Pearls on the Classics for Elementary Learning" in ten juan, "Jade Sea" in two hundred juan, "Guide to Literary Composition" in four juan, "Garden of Literary Examination Topics" in forty juan, "Quick Mastery Primer of Surnames" in six juan, "Investigation of Han Institutions" in four juan, "Compilation of Astronomy in the Six Classics" in six juan, and "Recitations for Elementary Learning" in four juan.
translations.idiomatic: Among his works were "Collected Works of Shenning" (100 juan), "Drafts from the Royal Hall" (23 juan), "Drafts from the Palace Secretariat" (22 juan), "Investigation of the Odes," "Geographical Investigation of the Odes," his verification of the Han bibliographic treatise, his geographic studies of the "Comprehensive Mirror," "Observations from Difficult Study," "Elementary Instruction," supplements to the "Quick Mastery Primer" and "Royal Assembly Chapter," "Pearls on the Classics for Elementary Learning," the encyclopedic "Jade Sea" (200 juan), guides to literary composition, surname primers, studies of Han institutions, astronomic compilations, and elementary recitations.

sentences.zh: 黃震，字東發，慶元府慈溪人。

translations.literal: Huang Zhen, styled Dongfa, a man of Cixi in Qingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhen, courtesy name Dongfa, was a native of Cixi in Qingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 寶祐四年登進士第，調吳縣尉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoyou he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoyou year 4 he passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as magistrate of Wu County.

sentences.zh: 吳多豪勢家，告私債則以屬尉，民多饑凍窘苦，死尉卒手。

translations.literal: Wu had many powerful families; when they reported private debts it was assigned to the sheriff, and the people, mostly hungry, cold, and in distress, died at the hands of sheriff's runners.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was full of powerful houses; private debt suits were handed to the sheriff, and common people, already hungry, cold, and desperate, died under his runners.

sentences.zh: 震至，不受貴家告。

translations.literal: When Zhen arrived, he did not accept reports from noble families.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhen took office, he refused petitions from great families.

sentences.zh: 府檄攝其縣。

translations.literal: The prefectural office ordered him to act as county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture ordered him to serve as acting county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 及攝長洲、華亭，皆有聲。

translations.literal: When he also served as acting magistrate of Changzhou and Huating, he had reputation in all cases.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as acting magistrate of Changzhou and Huating as well, he won praise everywhere he served.

sentences.zh: 浙東提舉常平王華甫辟主管帳司文字。

translations.literal: Wang Huafu, intendant of Changping in Zhedong East, recruited him as supervisor of accounts documentation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huafu, Zhedong intendant of the Changping granaries, engaged him to supervise account documents.

sentences.zh: 時錢庚孫守常，朱熠守平江，吳君擢守嘉興，皆倚嬖幸厲民。

translations.literal: At the time Qian Gengsun was prefect of Chang, Zhu Yi was prefect of Pingjiang, and Wu Junzhuo was prefect of Jiaxing — all relied on favorites to oppress the people.
translations.idiomatic: Then Qian Gengsun governed Changzhou, Zhu Yi governed Pingjiang, and Wu Junzhuo governed Jiaxing — each leaning on court favorites to harry the people.

sentences.zh: 華甫病革，強起劾罷三人，震讚之也。

translations.literal: Huafu was critically ill but forcibly rose to impeach and dismiss the three; Zhen praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Huafu, though gravely ill, forced himself up to impeach and remove all three; Zhen applauded him.

sentences.zh: 沿海製置司辟幹辦、提領浙西鹽事，不就。

translations.literal: The coastal commissioner recruited him as staff officer and supervisor of Zhexi West salt affairs — he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The coastal commissioner tried to appoint him staff officer overseeing Zhexi salt — he declined.

sentences.zh: 改辟提領鎮江轉般倉分司。

translations.literal: He was instead recruited as supervisor of the Zhenjiang transshipment granary sub-office.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted instead a post supervising the Zhenjiang transshipment granary.

sentences.zh: 公田法行，改提領官田所，言不便，不聽，復轉般倉職。

translations.literal: When the public-field law was implemented, he was changed to supervisor of the official-field office; he said it was inconvenient; they did not listen; he returned to the transshipment granary post.
translations.idiomatic: When the public-field law took effect he was shifted to the official-field office; he argued it was harmful, was ignored, and went back to the transshipment granary.

sentences.zh: 入為點校贍軍激賞酒庫所檢察官。

translations.literal: He entered court as inspector of the Commissary Army Stimulating-award Wine Depot.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as inspector of the army commissary's stimulating-award wine depot.

sentences.zh: 擢史館檢閱，與修寧宗、理宗兩朝《國史》、《實錄》。

translations.literal: Promoted to historiography examiner; he participated in compiling the "National History" and "Veritable Records" of the Ningzong and Lizong reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Raised to historiography examiner, he helped compile the "National History" and "Veritable Records" for the reigns of Ningzong and Lizong.

sentences.zh: 輪對，言當時之大弊，曰民窮，曰兵弱，曰財匱，曰士大夫無恥。

translations.literal: In a rotating audience he spoke of the greatest abuses of the time, saying: the people are exhausted; the army is weak; finances are depleted; scholar-officials are shameless.
translations.idiomatic: In a rotating audience he named the age's gravest ills: the people were ruined, the army feeble, the treasury empty, and the literati without shame.

sentences.zh: 乞罷給度僧人道士牒，使其徒老死即消弭之，收其田入，可以富軍國，紓民力。

translations.literal: He begged to stop issuing certificates to Buddhist monks and Daoist priests, so that when their followers die the institution would naturally cease; collecting their land into state revenue could enrich army and state and relieve the people's burden.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that ordination certificates for monks and priests be halted so the orders would die out naturally, and that their lands be seized to fund the army and ease the people.

sentences.zh: 時宮中建內道場，故首及此。

translations.literal: At the time an inner Buddhist chapel was being built in the palace — hence he first raised this.
translations.idiomatic: The palace was then building an inner Buddhist chapel, which is why he raised the issue first.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，批降三秩，即出國門。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; personally annotated a demotion of three ranks; he immediately left the capital gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, enraged, marked his record for demotion by three ranks, and Zhen at once departed the capital.

sentences.zh: 用諫官言，得寢。

translations.literal: Following remonstrance officials' words, this was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: On the remonstrance of censorial officials, the punishment was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 出通判廣德軍。

translations.literal: He went out as military administrator of Guangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as military vice-prefect of Guangde Army.

sentences.zh: 初，孝宗頒朱熹社倉法於天下，而廣德則官置此倉。

translations.literal: Initially Emperor Xiaozong had promulgated Zhu Xi's community granary law throughout the realm, but in Guangde the government directly managed this granary.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong had once spread Zhu Xi's community-granary system empire-wide, yet in Guangde the granary was run by officials.

sentences.zh: 民困於納息，至以息為本，而息皆橫取，民窮至自經。

translations.literal: The people were harassed by paying interest; eventually the interest became the principal, and the interest was all forcibly extracted; the people were so impoverished they hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: People were crushed paying interest until interest itself became principal and was extorted at will; some were driven to suicide.

sentences.zh: 人以為熹之法，不敢議。

translations.literal: People thought it was Xi's law and did not dare discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Because it bore Zhu Xi's name, no one dared criticize it.

sentences.zh: 震曰：“不然。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "That is not so.

sentences.zh: 法出於堯、舜、三代聖人，猶有變通，安有先儒為法，不思救其弊耶？

translations.literal: Even when laws come from Yao, Shun, and the sages of the Three Dynasties, there is still room for adaptation — how can there be a prior Confucian's law where one does not think to remedy its abuses?
translations.idiomatic: Laws from Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties sages still admit change — must a former master's institution be kept though it brings harm?

sentences.zh: 況熹法，社倉歸之於民，而官不得與。

translations.literal: Moreover in Xi's law, the community granary reverts to the people and officials may not participate.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, in Zhu Xi's system the granary belongs to the community, not the magistrate.

sentences.zh: 官雖不與，而終有納息之患。

translations.literal: Though officials do not participate, in the end there is still the harm of paying interest.
translations.idiomatic: Even without official meddling, the burden of interest remained.

sentences.zh: ”震為別買田六百畝，以其租代社倉息，約非凶年不貸，而貸者不取息。

translations.literal: " Zhen separately purchased six hundred mu of land and used its rent in place of community-granary interest; the rule was that except in famine years there would be no lending, and those who borrowed paid no interest.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen bought six hundred mu on his own and substituted its rent for granary interest; loans were made only in famine years and carried no interest.

sentences.zh: 郡有祠山廟，歲合江、淮之民禱祈者數十萬，其牲皆用牛。

translations.literal: The commandery had the Cishan Temple; each year several hundred thousand people from the Yangtze and Huai gathered to pray; all sacrifices used cattle.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture held the Cishan Temple, where each year hundreds of thousands from the Yangtze and Huai came to pray, sacrificing oxen.

sentences.zh: 郡惡少挾兵刃舞牲迎神為常，鬥爭致犯法。

translations.literal: Ruffians in the commandery regularly carried weapons and danced with sacrificial animals to welcome the god; brawls led to violations of law.
translations.idiomatic: Local rowdies habitually armed themselves and danced with sacrificial beasts to greet the deity, brawling until the law was broken.

sentences.zh: 其俗又有自嬰桎梏、自拷掠以徼福者。

translations.literal: The custom also had people who put shackles on themselves as infants and self-flogged to beg blessings.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a custom of men shackling themselves from infancy and beating their own flesh to win divine favor.

sentences.zh: 震見，問之，乃兵卒。

translations.literal: When Zhen saw this and questioned them, they turned out to be soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen questioned them and found they were soldiers.

sentences.zh: 責自狀其罪，卒曰：“本無罪。

translations.literal: He ordered them to confess their crimes in writing; the soldier said: "Originally I had no crime.
translations.idiomatic: He made them write out their offenses; one soldier said, "I have done nothing wrong.

sentences.zh: ”震曰：“爾罪多，不敢對人言，特告神以免罪耳。

translations.literal: " Zhen said: "Your crimes are many; you dare not speak of them to people — you only tell the god to avoid punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen replied, "Your crimes are many; you will not confess them to men, only to the god to escape blame.

sentences.zh: ”杖之示眾。

translations.literal: " He had them beaten before the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: " He had them flogged in public as an example.

sentences.zh: 又其俗有所謂埋藏會者，為坎於庭，深、廣皆五尺，以所祭牛及器皿數百納其中，覆以牛革，封鐍一夕，明發視之，失所在。

translations.literal: The custom also had what was called the "Burial Assembly": they dug a pit in the courtyard five chi deep and wide, placed the sacrificed ox and several hundred vessels within, covered with ox hide, sealed with a lock overnight — at dawn when they looked, all was gone.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the "Burial Assembly": a five-foot pit was dug in the courtyard, the sacrificial ox and hundreds of vessels were placed inside, covered with hide and locked overnight — by morning everything had vanished.

sentences.zh: 震以為妖，而殺牛淫祀非法，言之諸司，禁絕之。

translations.literal: Zhen considered this sorcery, and killing cattle for illicit sacrifice was illegal; he reported it to the relevant offices and forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen judged it sorcery and unlawful ox sacrifice, reported it to the authorities, and banned it.

sentences.zh: 郡守賈蕃世以權相從子驕縱不法，震數與爭論是非，蕃世積不堪，疏震撓政，坐解官。

translations.literal: Prefect Jia Fanshi, nephew of the powerful chief councillor, was insolent and lawless; Zhen repeatedly debated right and wrong with him; Fanshi could not bear it and memorialized that Zhen obstructed government; he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Jia Fanshi, nephew of the reigning chief councillor, was arrogant and unruly; Zhen often crossed him; Fanshi, unable to endure it, accused Zhen of obstructing rule, and Zhen was removed.

sentences.zh: 尋通判紹興府，獲海寇，僇之。

translations.literal: Soon he was military administrator of Shaoxing Prefecture; he captured pirates and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he served as military vice-prefect of Shaoxing, seized pirates, and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 撫州饑起，震知其州，單車疾馳，中道約富人耆老集城中，毋過某日。

translations.literal: Famine riot arose in Fuzhou; Zhen was appointed prefect; he rode alone at speed; midway he summoned wealthy men and elders to assemble in the city — none past a certain day.
translations.idiomatic: When famine sparked unrest in Fuzhou, Zhen was named prefect; he galloped ahead alone and, on the road, ordered rich men and elders to gather in the city by a set day.

sentences.zh: 至則大書“閉糶者藉，強糴者斬”揭於市，坐驛舍署文書，不入州治，不抑米價，價日損。

translations.literal: On arrival he posted in large characters "Those who hoard grain shall be punished; those who forcibly buy grain shall be beheaded" in the market; he sat in the post station handling documents, not entering the prefectural headquarters, not suppressing rice prices — prices daily fell.
translations.idiomatic: Arriving, he posted in the market, "Hoarders will be punished; forced buyers will be executed"; he worked from the courier station, never entering the yamen or fixing prices, and rice fell day by day.

sentences.zh: 親煮粥食餓者。

translations.literal: He personally cooked porridge to feed the starving.
translations.idiomatic: He himself boiled gruel for the hungry.

sentences.zh: 請於朝，給爵賞旌勞者，而後入視州事。

translations.literal: He requested from court titles and rewards to honor the laborers; only then did he enter to conduct prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the court for honors for those who had helped, and only then took up regular prefectural duties.

sentences.zh: 轉運司下州糴米七萬石，震曰：“民生蹶矣，豈宜重困之！

translations.literal: The transport commission ordered the prefecture to purchase seventy thousand shi of rice; Zhen said: "The people's livelihood has already stumbled — how can we further heavily burden them!
translations.idiomatic: The transport office demanded the prefecture buy seventy thousand shi of rice; Zhen said, "The people are already prostrate — how can we crush them again!

sentences.zh: ”以沒官田三莊所入應之。

translations.literal: " He met this with income from three confiscated official estates.
translations.idiomatic: " He covered the quota with revenue from three seized official estates.

sentences.zh: 若補刻《六經》、《儀禮》，修復朱熹祠，樹晏殊裏門曰“舊學坊”，製祭社稷器，復風雷祀，勸民種麥，禁競渡船，焚千三百餘艘，用其丁鐵創軍營五百間，皆善政也。

translations.literal: He also supplemented carved editions of the "Six Classics" and "Rites of Zhou," restored Zhu Xi's shrine, marked Yan Shu's home gate "Old Study Lane," made ritual vessels for state and earth sacrifice, restored wind-and-thunder worship, encouraged people to plant wheat, forbade racing boats — burning over thirteen hundred vessels, using their labor and iron to build five hundred military barracks rooms — all were good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He reprinted the "Six Classics" and "Rites of Zhou," restored Zhu Xi's temple, labeled Yan Shu's gate "Old Study Lane," made vessels for the altars of soil and grain, revived wind-and-thunder rites, urged wheat planting, outlawed racing boats — burning more than thirteen hundred craft and using their timber and iron for five hundred barracks — all worthy acts.

sentences.zh: 詔增秩，遂升提舉常平倉司。

translations.literal: An edict raised his rank; he was then promoted intendant of the Changping Granary Office.
translations.idiomatic: The throne increased his rank and promoted him intendant of the Changping granaries.

sentences.zh: 舊有結關拒逮捕事係郡獄二十有八年，存者十無三四，以事關尚書省，無敢決其獄者，以結關為作亂也。

translations.literal: There was an old case of forming associations to resist arrest imprisoned in the prefecture for twenty-eight years; of those who survived, barely three or four in ten; because the matter concerned the Ministry of Personnel no one dared decide the case — they treated association-forming as rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: A twenty-eight-year-old case of men who banded together to resist arrest still filled the jail; fewer than three or four in ten remained alive; because the Ministry of Personnel was involved, no judge would rule — banding together was treated as revolt.

sentences.zh: 震謂結關猶他郡之結甲也，非作亂比，況已經數赦，於是皆釋之。

translations.literal: Zhen said forming associations was like forming mutual-aid groups elsewhere — not comparable to rebellion; moreover several amnesties had passed; he therefore released them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen held that such leagues resembled mutual-aid societies elsewhere, not rebellion, and that repeated amnesties had covered them; he freed them all.

sentences.zh: 新城與光澤地犬牙相入，民夾溪而處，歲常忿鬥爭漁。

translations.literal: Xincheng and Guangze territories interlocked; people lived on both banks of a stream; each year they frequently fought over fishing rights.
translations.idiomatic: Xincheng and Guangze bordered each other; villagers on both sides of a creek fought every year over fishing grounds.

sentences.zh: 會知縣事蹇雄為政擾民，因相結拒，起焚掠。

translations.literal: When acting magistrate Jian Xiong's governance harassed the people, they formed associations to resist, then rose to burn and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: When acting magistrate Jian Xiong oppressed them, the people banded together, then rioted, burning and looting.

sentences.zh: 震乃劾罷雄，諭其民散去。

translations.literal: Zhen impeached and removed Xiong and instructed the people to disperse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen impeached Xiong, removed him, and ordered the crowd to go home.

sentences.zh: 初，常平有慈幼局，為貧而棄子者設，久而名存實亡。

translations.literal: Initially the Changping office had a Charity for Infants Bureau, established for the poor who abandoned children — over time the name remained but the reality vanished.
translations.idiomatic: The Changping office once ran a Charity for Infants for the poor who cast away children, but the name survived after the work ceased.

sentences.zh: 震謂收哺於既棄之後，不若先其未棄保全之。

translations.literal: Zhen said collecting and nurturing after abandonment was inferior to preserving them before abandonment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen argued that rescuing babies after abandonment was worse than keeping families from abandoning them at all.

sentences.zh: 乃損益舊法，凡當免而貧者，許裏胥請於官贍之，棄者許人收養，官出粟給所收家，成活者眾。

translations.literal: He then revised the old law: all who should be exempted but were poor could have neighborhood officers request official support; those abandoned could be adopted by others; the government supplied grain to the adopting household — many children survived.
translations.idiomatic: He reworked the rules: poor families entitled to exemption could ask officials for aid through neighborhood clerks; abandoned infants could be adopted with state grain paid to the foster home — and many lived.

sentences.zh: 震論役法，先令縣核民產業，不使下戶受抑於上戶。

translations.literal: Zhen discussed the corvée law, first ordering counties to verify the people's property so that lower households would not be oppressed by upper households.
translations.idiomatic: On corvée service, Zhen had counties assess household wealth first so poor families would not be burdened by the rich.

sentences.zh: 大興水利，廢陂、壞堰及為豪右所占者，復之。

translations.literal: He greatly promoted waterworks, restoring abandoned reservoirs, broken dikes, and those seized by powerful elites.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed irrigation hard, restoring ruined ponds, broken dams, and works seized by local magnates.

sentences.zh: 改提點刑獄，決滯獄，清民訟，赫然如神明。

translations.literal: Transferred to judicial intendant, he cleared backlogged cases, settled the people's lawsuits, and shone in judgment like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Made judicial intendant, he cleared stale prisons, untangled civil suits, and judged with awesome clarity.

sentences.zh: 有貴家害民，震按之，貴家怨。

translations.literal: When a noble house harmed the people, Zhen investigated them; the noble house resented it.
translations.idiomatic: He prosecuted a great family that had wronged commoners, and they bore him a grudge.

sentences.zh: 又強發富人粟與民，富人亦怨。

translations.literal: He also forcibly requisitioned grain from the wealthy to give to the people; the wealthy also resented it.
translations.idiomatic: He also compelled rich men to release grain to the hungry, and they too turned against him.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞陳堅以讒者言，劾震去，讒者，乃怨震者也。

translations.literal: Vice censor-in-chief Chen Jian, on the words of slanderers, impeached Zhen and removed him — the slanderers were those who resented Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Chen Jian, acting on accusers' reports, impeached Zhen from office — the accusers were men who hated him.

sentences.zh: 遂奉雲台祠。

translations.literal: He then received appointment at the Yuntai Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He was then given a sinecure at the Yuntai Shrine.

sentences.zh: 賈似道罷相，以宗正寺簿召，將與俞浙並為監察御史，有內戚畏震直，止之，而浙亦以直言去。

translations.literal: When Jia Sidao was dismissed as chief councillor, Zhen was summoned as registrar of the Court of Imperial Clan; he was to be made censor alongside Yu Zhe — a palace relative, fearing Zhen's bluntness, stopped it, and Zhe also left on account of straight speech.
translations.idiomatic: After Jia Sidao left the chief ministership, Zhen was recalled as registrar in the Court of Imperial Clan and slated to become censor with Yu Zhe; a consort's kin, dreading Zhen's candor, blocked the move, and Zhe likewise departed for speaking plainly.

sentences.zh: 移浙東提舉常平，鎮安饑民，折盜賊萌芽。

translations.literal: Transferred to Zhedong intendant of the Changping granaries, he pacified hungry people and cut off budding banditry.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhedong intendant of Changping granaries, he settled famine refugees and stamped out incipient robbery.

sentences.zh: 時皇叔大父福王與芮判紹興府，遂兼王府長史。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor's grand-uncle, Prince Fu Wang Yuru, served as prefect of Shaoxing Prefecture; Zhen was therefore also made chief administrator of the princely household.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's grand-uncle, Prince Fu Yuru, was then prefect of Shaoxing, so Zhen was also named chief administrator of the princely household.

sentences.zh: 震奏曰：“朝廷之製，尊卑不同，而紀綱不可紊。

translations.literal: Zhen memorialized: "In the court's institutions, high and low differ, yet standards must not be confused.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen wrote, "Court protocol distinguishes rank, but the norms must not be broken.

sentences.zh: 外雖藩王，監司得言之。

translations.literal: Outwardly one may be a feudal prince, yet a supervisory commissioner may speak of his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Even a prince in the provinces may be criticized by a circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 今為其屬，豈敢察其非，奈何自臣復壞其法？

translations.literal: Now to become his subordinate — how would I dare inspect his wrongdoing? Why should I myself again ruin this law?
translations.idiomatic: If I serve under him, how can I investigate his faults? Why should I be the one to undermine the rule?

sentences.zh: ”固不拜長史。

translations.literal: " He firmly refused to accept the post of chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: " He steadfastly declined the chief administrator's appointment.

sentences.zh: 命進侍左郎官及宗正少卿，皆不拜。

translations.literal: Ordered to advance to attendant of the Left and vice director of the Court of Imperial Clan — he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered promoted to attendant of the Left and vice director of the Court of Imperial Clan, and again refused both posts.

sentences.zh: 震嚐告人曰：“非聖人之書不可觀，無益之詩文不作可也。

translations.literal: Zhen once told others: "Books that are not those of sages should not be read; useless poetry and prose need not be written.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen once said, "Read only the sages; write no poetry or prose that does no good.

sentences.zh: ”居官恒未明視事，事至立決。

translations.literal: " In office he always began work before dawn; when affairs arrived he decided them at once.
translations.idiomatic: " In office he rose before daylight; when a case came in, he settled it on the spot.

sentences.zh: 自奉儉薄，人有急難，則周之，不少吝。

translations.literal: He lived frugally on meager means; when others had urgent distress he would aid them without stinting.
translations.idiomatic: He kept himself poor and spare, yet when anyone faced crisis he helped generously.

sentences.zh: 所著《日抄》一百卷。

translations.literal: His writing included "Daily Notes" in one hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: He authored "Daily Notes" in one hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 卒，門人私諡曰文潔先生。

translations.literal: He died; his disciples privately gave him the posthumous title Master Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his students privately honored him as Master Wenjie.
